title: General NP witness encryption from plain LWE
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Can we build a witness encryption scheme for arbitrary NP relations, polynomial-time and secure, relying only on the standard decisional LWE assumption? The scheme should specify modulus, noise, and hardness parameters explicitly, without evasive or knowledge assumptions.
status: This has been a central frontier since 2013. Evasive-LWE candidates (Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs, 2022, [Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140)) and schemes for special languages do not settle the question. The problem traces to Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258).
solved_when: A polynomial-time witness encryption scheme for every NP relation is constructed and proven secure under plain decisional LWE alone, with explicit modulus, noise, and hardness parameters and no evasive or knowledge assumptions.
why: It would give general encrypt-to-condition a widely studied lattice foundation, replacing the current reliance on stronger or less standard assumptions.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258); Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140).

title: Polynomial-hardness-only algebraic WE
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Can witness encryption for general NP relations be built from only polynomially hard algebraic assumptions — polynomial-hardness versions of DLIN, large-field LPN, and binary sparse LPN — rather than subexponential hardness? In other words, can the subexponential hardness requirement be eliminated without paying an exponential overhead in algorithmic efficiency?
status: This is a proposed weakening of the assumptions underlying the 2024 algebraic iO construction of Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856); no such polynomial-hardness-only construction is currently known.
solved_when: A construction of general witness encryption is given whose security reduces to polynomial hardness of DLIN, large-field LPN, and binary sparse LPN, with no subexponential hardness assumption and no exponential algorithmic overhead.
why: It would weaken the assumptions needed for witness encryption and avoid the security-parameter inflation that subexponential-hardness assumptions force, yielding a more practical foundation for the underlying obfuscation program.
key_works: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: Witness encryption from one-way functions
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Can general witness encryption be constructed assuming only the existence of one-way functions? The construction may need to use the one-way function's code non-black-boxly; alternatively, one may aim to establish a barrier to such a construction that goes beyond the existing black-box separations.
status: The problem has been discussed since 2013, when witness encryption was introduced by Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258). It is known that witness encryption combined with one-way functions implies public-key encryption.
solved_when: Either a construction of general witness encryption from arbitrary one-way functions (possibly non-black-box) is given, or a suitably qualified impossibility result is proved that rules out such constructions beyond known black-box separations.
why: It would tie conditional encryption to the most minimal conventional computational secrecy assumption, and it is known that witness encryption together with one-way functions already implies public-key encryption — placing the question squarely on the path from symmetric to public-key primitives.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258).

title: Perfect correctness from negligible decryption error
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Can any witness encryption scheme with negligible decryption error be transformed, without strengthening its assumptions, into one with perfect correctness — or is there a fundamental barrier for some complete NP relation?
status: The question lies outside the scope of the March 2026 equivalence of Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download); repetition reduces the decryption error but does not eliminate it.
solved_when: Either an assumption-preserving compiler from negligibly incorrect witness encryption to perfectly correct witness encryption is given, or a barrier is proven for a specified complete NP relation.
why: It determines whether exceptional encryption randomness can permanently strand valid rewards or archives, or whether such losses can always be compiled away.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Remove special-honest-verifier simulation
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Can an ordinary honest-verifier zero-knowledge argument with logarithmic prover communication yield witness encryption, without relying on the stronger special-honest-verifier simulation paradigm? Formally, does the known equivalence between such laconic arguments and witness encryption survive when the simulation is not conditioned on a supplied verifier random tape?
status: The 2026 equivalence of Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download), is proved using SHVZK; ordinary HVZK is explicitly distinguished from it in that work, and the gap remains open.
solved_when: Witness encryption is constructed from logarithmic-prover-communication ordinary HVZK arguments — i.e., the 2026 equivalence is reestablished with ordinary HVZK in place of SHVZK — or a separation showing ordinary HVZK does not suffice is proved.
why: It would unlock witness encryption from a substantially wider collection of zero-knowledge protocols, since many natural protocols are only ordinary HVZK.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Tight quantitative laconic-to-WE transformations
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Can the known transformation from laconic argument systems to witness encryption be made quantitatively tight, with encryption cost, ciphertext size, and security loss depending optimally on the transcript support size and the soundness gap? A satisfactory answer would match the unavoidable input and output costs of the underlying proof system rather than merely preserving polynomial equivalence.
status: Currently only a qualitative polynomial-equivalence theorem is known, due to Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download); the quantitative target above remains open.
solved_when: A transformation is given whose encryption cost, ciphertext size, and security loss are tight (up to constants or lower-order factors) in the transcript support and soundness gap, matching the unavoidable input and output costs.
why: It determines whether proof-system characterizations of witness encryption can become useful constructions rather than merely equivalence statements.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: All-length public-key encryption from weak NP hardness and WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can public-key encryption be secured at every sufficiently large length from the same premises that are currently known to give it only infinitely often — namely a nonuniform witness encryption scheme plus NP ⊄ BPP? Equivalently, upgrade the infinitely-often conclusion to standard all-length security without strengthening the assumptions.
status: The cited route — Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34), building on Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download) — yields only infinitely-often security; stronger hardness premises are known to support stronger conclusions.
solved_when: A construction of public-key encryption secure at every sufficiently large security parameter is given, assuming only nonuniform witness encryption and NP ⊄ BPP.
why: It would turn sparse-length cryptographic existence results into the conventional, deployable asymptotic security notion used throughout cryptography.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download).

title: Complete characterization of zero-test leakage
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: What algebraic information do all legal zero tests in a proposed witness-encryption encoding expose? A complete answer would characterize the leakage of every admissible zero test, including combinations that lack low-level zero encodings.
status: Attacks since 2015 show that eliminating obvious zero encodings is insufficient; key works include Coron et al. (2015), [Zeroizing Without Low-Level Zeroes: New MMAP Attacks and Their Limitations](https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/596), and Cheon et al. (2015), [Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/906).
solved_when: An explicit characterization exists of the algebraic information leaked by all legal zero tests in proposed WE encodings, covering combinations without low-level zero encodings.
why: It would replace the current patch-by-patch defense approach with an explicit leakage boundary for these constructions.
key_works: Coron et al. (2015), [Zeroizing Without Low-Level Zeroes: New MMAP Attacks and Their Limitations](https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/596); Cheon et al. (2015), [Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/906).

title: Better exponents for nontrivial exponential WE
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Can we build standard-assumption witness encryption whose encryption time improves the exponent over brute-force enumeration of witnesses, while keeping the construction in its claimed nontriviality regime?
status: Nontrivial exponential-time constructions have existed since 2018, due to Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs, [Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874); achieving polynomial time is a different frontier.
solved_when: A construction from standard assumptions is given whose encryption-time exponent strictly beats the brute-force exponent of enumerating witnesses, and the nontriviality regime of the prior nontrivial exponential-time constructions is preserved.
why: Better exponents may make bounded-size applications of witness encryption practical before a fully efficient general scheme is achieved.
key_works: Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs (2018), [Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874).

title: Annihilating FHE without the ideal-cipher model
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Can the annihilating-FHE route to witness encryption be instantiated in the standard model, without the ideal-cipher model, while preserving the security properties the construction requires?
status: This is a proposed model-removal target following the 2020/2021 construction framework of Kluczniak (2020/2021), [Witness Encryption from Garbled Circuit and Multikey Fully Homomorphic Encryption Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1502); no standard-model instantiation is known.
solved_when: A standard-model annihilating-FHE-based witness encryption scheme is given whose required security properties are proven under an explicit assumption, replacing the ideal-cipher component of the 2020/2021 construction framework.
why: It replaces an idealized component with an explicit assumption and an actual implementation, making the witness-encryption construction concretely realizable.
key_works: Kluczniak (2020/2021), [Witness Encryption from Garbled Circuit and Multikey Fully Homomorphic Encryption Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1502).

title: KZG-opening EWE outside the algebraic group model
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Can extractable witness encryption for KZG commitments be proven secure in a model where the adversary accesses only the concrete group, without the algebraic-group assumption that it always provides an algebraic representation of its queries? In other words, establish EWE for KZG openings with comparable efficiency outside the algebraic group model.
status: The construction of Fleischhacker–Hall-Andersen–Simkin (2024), [Extractable Witness Encryption for KZG Commitments and Efficient Laconic OT](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/264), achieves a one-group-element ciphertext, but its extractability is proven only in its algebraic model.
solved_when: A proof of extractable witness encryption for KZG openings in a concrete (non-algebraic) group model is given, with a ciphertext retaining the efficiency of the 2024 construction — namely one group element.
why: It would place one of the most efficient special-language witness-encryption examples on a foundation that does not grant the adversary's algebraic-representation access, closing the gap between the current model and standard concrete-group assumptions.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Hall-Andersen–Simkin (2024), [Extractable Witness Encryption for KZG Commitments and Efficient Laconic OT](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/264).

title: WE gadgets for nonlinear verifiers
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Can we build efficient witness-encryption gadgets whose verifiers cover genuinely nonlinear relations, without falling back on interaction or general indistinguishability obfuscation to handle the hard parts?
status: The 2025/2026 framework of Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025/2026), [A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364), handles linearly verifiable SNARK structure; nonlinear parts remain consequential.
solved_when: Explicit efficient WE gadgets are constructed for nonlinear verifier relations (e.g., beyond pairing-product equations), replacing no portion of the relation with interaction or general iO.
why: It broadens practical proof-conditioned encryption beyond the linearly verifiable setting.
key_works: Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025/2026), [A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).

title: Remove short-solution promises without stronger knowledge assumptions
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Can special-language lattice extractable witness encryption be built for naturally generated instances, without the restrictive promise that solutions are short? A satisfactory answer would remove the homogeneous short-solution promise while resting only on a knowledge assumption of comparable strength to those currently used.
status: The 2022–2023 constructions supply important restricted baselines: Choi–Vaudenay (2022), [Towards Witness Encryption Without Multilinear Maps](https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/295725/files/978-3-031-08896-4_2.pdf); Tran–Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9).
solved_when: A construction of extractable witness encryption for the special lattice language is given that works on unpromised (naturally generated) instances, and whose underlying extractability/knowledge assumption is no stronger in kind than the assumptions supporting the promised-case constructions.
why: It would extend lattice-based witness encryption from artificially promised instances to those arising naturally, making the primitive usable in realistic settings.
key_works: Choi–Vaudenay (2022), [Towards Witness Encryption Without Multilinear Maps](https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/295725/files/978-3-031-08896-4_2.pdf); Tran–Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9).

title: UP witness PRFs without evasive LWE
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Can the unique-witness (UP) route to witness PRFs be re-founded on a well-studied, falsifiable assumption instead of evasive LWE? Formally, is there a construction of witness PRFs for UP languages whose security rests on a standard assumption rather than evasive LWE?
status: The premise was weakened by counterexamples: Döttling et al. (2025), [Simple and General Counterexamples for Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/374), showed private-coin evasive LWE fails, making the foundation repair proposed here more pressing. The UP route itself originates with Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227).
solved_when: A witness PRF construction for UP languages is given, with a security proof from a well-studied falsifiable assumption, replacing the evasive-LWE premise entirely.
why: It preserves the unique-witness strategy for SNARKs under a more stable assumption base, keeping the standard-assumption program for UP alive now that evasive LWE itself is in question.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227); Döttling et al. (2025), [Simple and General Counterexamples for Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/374).

title: Bounded-ambiguity witness PRFs
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Can witness PRFs, currently built for relations with unique witnesses, be extended to relations having only a bounded number of witnesses while keeping the function's output independent of which witness is used? Formally, construct witness PRFs for languages in an intermediate class between UP and unrestricted NP where the witness set size is polynomially bounded.
status: Proposed as an intermediate expressivity target between UP and unrestricted NP. The starting point is Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227). Related notions include FewP, isolation lemmas, and ambiguity hierarchies.
solved_when: A construction of witness PRFs (with witness-independent output) is given for all NP relations whose witness sets have bounded size, under standard assumptions, with a proof of correctness and pseudorandomness.
why: It captures naturally ambiguous credentials and proofs, where multiple valid witnesses exist for a single statement, extending the applicability of witness PRFs beyond unique-witness settings.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227).

title: Polynomial-loss adaptive UP arguments
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Can the adaptive soundness of the UP argument route be proved with only a polynomial loss in the underlying hardness assumption, replacing the exponential loss that current techniques incur?
status: The problem is a proposed quantitative improvement to the 2024 framework; no such polynomial-loss reduction is currently known. Key work: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227). Related directions include tight adaptive soundness and complexity leveraging.
solved_when: A reduction is exhibited for the relevant UP argument route whose security loss is polynomial rather than exponential, within the 2024 Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan framework.
why: An exponential loss forces the underlying hardness assumption to be disproportionately strong; a polynomial-loss reduction removes that requirement.
key_works: Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Adaptively Sound Zero-Knowledge SNARKs for UP](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/227).

title: Delegatable witness PRFs below iO
subfield: Witness PRFs and witness maps
open: Can we construct witness PRFs whose public evaluation keys can delegate restricted evaluation authority — producing compact keys for descendants — while remaining collusion-resistant, all under assumptions strictly weaker than general indistinguishability obfuscation?
status: The problem is a proposed extension of witness PRFs and constrained evaluation, suggested against the backdrop of Zhandry (2014/2016), [How to Avoid Obfuscation Using Witness PRFs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/301); related directions include delegatable constrained PRFs and hierarchical functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction of delegatable witness PRFs exists with compact descendant keys and proven collusion resistance, under an assumption below general iO.
why: Such a primitive would support hierarchical agent and organizational capabilities built from witness PRFs.
key_works: Zhandry (2014/2016), [How to Avoid Obfuscation Using Witness PRFs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/301).

title: Adaptive offline WE from plain WE and LWE
subfield: Offline, batched, positional, and signature-based WE
open: Can fully adaptive offline witness encryption be built from plain witness encryption together with LWE, while keeping online work near-linear and preprocessing explicitly amortized? Formally, the goal is a construction meeting the combined assumption-and-cost target that existing semi-adaptive and adaptive results each achieve only in part.
status: Semi-adaptive and adaptive offline results exist under their respective premises; the combined assumption-and-cost target above is strictly stronger. Key works: Pal–Dutta (2020), [Semi-Adaptively Secure Offline Witness Encryption from Puncturable Witness PRF](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/479); Liu et al. (2023), [适应性安全的离线证据加密](https://www.jos.org.cn/jos/article/abstract/6423).
solved_when: A construction of fully adaptive offline witness encryption from plain WE plus LWE is given, with near-linear online work and explicit amortization of preprocessing costs.
why: A solution makes previously unknown conditions cheap to encrypt after preprocessing.
key_works: Pal–Dutta (2020), [Semi-Adaptively Secure Offline Witness Encryption from Puncturable Witness PRF](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/479); Liu et al. (2023), [适应性安全的离线证据加密](https://www.jos.org.cn/jos/article/abstract/6423).

title: QCMA-WE without full QMA machinery
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Can witness encryption for QCMA — classical witnesses checked by quantum verifiers — be constructed from post-quantum NP witness encryption plus weaker additions than general quantum obfuscation? In other words, is there a path to this intermediate encryption notion that avoids the full QMA-style machinery?
status: This is a proposed intermediate model; the key difficulty is that classical witness strings do not turn quantum verification into an NP relation. Related work includes Bartusek–Malavolta (2022), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation of Null Quantum Circuits and Applications](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2022.15).
solved_when: A construction of witness encryption for QCMA languages is given, building on post-quantum NP-WE and ingredients strictly weaker than general quantum obfuscation, with correctness and semantic security proven.
why: It would capture a potentially easier and still useful class of quantum-verification statements, filling the gap between NP and full QMA witness encryption.
key_works: Bartusek–Malavolta (2022), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation of Null Quantum Circuits and Applications](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2022.15).

title: Remove subexponential FE from the QPrO route
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Can quantum null obfuscation (or QMA witness encryption) be built within the QPrO route assuming only polynomially secure functional encryption, with a reduction that loses at most polynomial factors? That is, can the subexponential-security assumption in the current ideal-obfuscation theorem be weakened to standard polynomial security?
status: The existing ideal-obfuscation theorem assumes subexponentially secure functional encryption. Key works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).
solved_when: A theorem is proved deriving quantum null obfuscation or QMA-WE in the QPrO setting from polynomially secure functional encryption via a reduction with polynomial loss.
why: It weakens the quantitative strength of the underlying premise, making the construction's security assumption standard rather than subexponential.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Statistical quantum-WE language classification
subfield: Quantum language classes and witness resources
open: Which promise languages admit statistical quantum witness encryption — and does the answer differ between classical and quantum ciphertexts, or between general and efficiently samplable quantum witnesses? A formal characterization of these classes, beyond what general statistical quantum obfuscation already implies, is the target.
status: The problem is proposed as a classification question; it is known that consequences of general statistical quantum obfuscation do not automatically characterize the weaker WE setting. Key works: Alagic–Fefferman (2016), [On Quantum Obfuscation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01771); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/). Related threads include quantum statistical zero knowledge and complexity collapses.
solved_when: A complete classification is given of the promise languages admitting statistical quantum witness encryption in each setting considered — classical ciphertexts versus quantum ciphertexts, and unrestricted versus efficiently samplable quantum witnesses.
why: It identifies the information-theoretic security conditions quantum mechanics makes possible for witness encryption, and clarifies which languages fall outside the reach of obfuscation-derived results.
key_works: Alagic–Fefferman (2016), [On Quantum Obfuscation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01771); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/).

title: The Minicrypt range-avoidance conjecture
subfield: Further named complexity conjectures
open: Do one-way functions and NP≠coNP suffice to show that the range-avoidance problem Avoid — given a stretching circuit, output a string outside its range — cannot be solved in FP? A proposed route replaces strong-WE-derived predictable arguments with sufficient arguments obtained from one-way functions alone.
status: Explicit Conjecture 5.1 of Ren–Wang–Zhong, revised March 2026. Strong-WE and demi-bit results provide partial foundations; the one-way-function premise remains unresolved. Key works: Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061); Faonio–Nielsen–Venturi (2017), [Predictable Arguments of Knowledge](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-54365-8_6).
solved_when: It is proved that one-way functions together with NP≠coNP imply Avoid∉FP.
why: It would connect minimal cryptographic hardness (mere one-way functions) to explicit search lower bounds and proof-complexity consequences for range avoidance.
key_works: Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061); Faonio–Nielsen–Venturi (2017), [Predictable Arguments of Knowledge](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-54365-8_6).

title: Fully succinct cutoff-iO from rate-one null-iO
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Can cutoff indistinguishability obfuscation be made fully succinct, with output length polynomial in the security parameter, the circuit size, and \(\log N\), under rate-one null-iO and LWE? A sharper phrasing: remove the multiplicative growth of function-binding hash keys and openings that compounds across recursion levels in the existing compiler.
status: The problem is stated explicitly by Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026); substituting rate-one null-iO into their compiler still permits only constantly many recursion levels. Reference: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).
solved_when: A cutoff-iO construction is given whose output length is polynomial in \(\lambda\), the circuit size, and \(\log N\), assuming rate-one null-iO and LWE, with no multiplicative blowup of function-binding hash keys and openings across recursion levels.
why: A solution isolates and resolves the compiler-level obstruction, cleanly separating it from the independent task of constructing rate-one null-iO itself.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Fully adaptive circuit registered ABE from plain WE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can registered attribute-based encryption for polynomial-size circuits, built from plain witness encryption and LWE, be upgraded to fully adaptive security — where corruption choices may depend on the public parameters and prior registrations, including admissible later corruption of honest users — while preserving succinct master and helper keys? A polynomial-loss reduction is required, and adaptive challenge-policy selection alone is insufficient.
status: This is a proposed strengthening of Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023); the 2026 comparison still classifies this WE-based construction as static, though adaptive ordinary broadcast encryption was separately achieved in 2025. Key works: Cody Freitag, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812); Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).
solved_when: A construction from plain WE and LWE achieves registered ABE for polynomial-size circuits with adaptive security (corruptions adaptive over public parameters and previous registrations, with admissible later corruption of honest users), a polynomial reduction loss, and succinct master and helper keys preserved.
why: It would support securely changing registered populations and adversarial compromise after deployment, where current static-security guarantees do not apply.
key_works: Cody Freitag, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812); Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Adaptive linear-CRS pairing registered ABE in the plain model
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can we build a registered ABE scheme for monotone span programs, in the plain model, that achieves fully adaptive security while keeping a common reference string of linear size \(O(N)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\)? Formally, the goal is adaptive security under polynomially hard, explicitly stated pairing assumptions, without random oracles and without an a priori policy-size bound introduced solely by complexity leveraging.
status: The gap was proposed after Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), who proved linear-CRS static security in the plain model; their adaptive variant requires random oracles, a policy-size bound, and subexponential hardness. Key work: Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-35367-2_13); [full version](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).
solved_when: A registered ABE scheme for monotone span programs is proven fully adaptively secure in the plain model (no random oracles) under polynomially hard, explicitly stated pairing assumptions, with a CRS of size \(O(N)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) and no a priori policy-size bound arising from complexity leveraging.
why: It would combine the setup savings of a linear-size CRS with adaptive security while relying only on weaker, polynomial quantitative assumptions — removing the random oracles, policy bounds, and subexponential hardness currently needed for adaptivity.
key_works: Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-35367-2_13); [full version](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Multi-authority registered ABE from plain WE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can we build multi-authority registered attribute-based encryption supporting general polynomial-size monotone circuits for an unbounded registered population, using only ordinary witness encryption and LWE — while preserving independent curators, transparent aggregation, and resistance to combining attributes of different users across authorities?
status: Proposed as an assumption-reduction target following Lu–Waters–Wu (2025); their unbounded expressive construction uses iO and function-binding hashes, while their pairing construction bounds the population and supports only linear-secret-sharing policies.
solved_when: A construction is given, from plain witness encryption plus LWE, achieving multi-authority registered ABE for general polynomial-size monotone circuits with an a priori unbounded registered population, independent curators, transparent aggregation, and cross-authority collusion resistance.
why: It would extend encrypt-to-condition across autonomous organizations without centralizing key issuance, removing the need for the iO or bounded-population/pairing assumptions of current schemes.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2025), [Multi-Authority Registered Attribute-Based Encryption](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1279); Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812).

title: Public verification from designated-verifier witness maps
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Can a publicly verifiable unique witness map for NP be built from witness PRFs, with computational soundness, or are these primitives genuinely separable? The map's output must depend only on the statement, even though evaluation is given an arbitrary valid witness.
status: A 2023 implication map proposed the converse direction: public unique witness maps imply witness PRFs, while designated-verifier unique witness maps are equivalent to witness PRFs (Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343)).
solved_when: A construction of a publicly verifiable, computationally sound unique witness map for NP from witness PRFs is given, or a separation between witness PRFs and public unique witness maps is proved — in either case with output depending only on the statement despite arbitrary valid witnesses on input.
why: It would turn witness-gated pseudorandom evaluation into canonical proofs that anyone can check.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).
aliases: WPRF-to-UWM implication; publicizing designated-verifier unique witness maps.

title: Negligible-error canonicalization of compact witness maps
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Can a witness map whose statements have at most \(2^{O(\log\lambda)}\) possible outputs be converted into a pseudo-unique witness map with negligible canonical-output failure and polynomial setup and evaluation? The conversion must also account for setup-dependent failure modes that repetition under a single CRS cannot eliminate.
status: The problem is a proposed quantitative strengthening of Chakraborty–Prabhakaran–Wichs (2023), whose conversion achieves success \(1-1/p(\lambda)\) for any chosen polynomial \(p\); see Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).
solved_when: A conversion is exhibited achieving canonical-output failure negligible in \(\lambda\) (rather than \(1-1/p(\lambda)\) for a chosen polynomial \(p\)), with polynomial-time setup and evaluation, for witness maps with at most \(2^{O(\log\lambda)}\) possible outputs per statement.
why: It would yield canonical evidence reusable across many conditional-encryption applications without committing to an inverse-polynomial error budget.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).

title: Mildly compact witness maps from ordinary NIZKs
subfield: Witness maps, witness PRFs, and proof canonicalization
open: Can deterministic witness maps with at most \(2^{p(\lambda)}\) outputs per statement be built from just ordinary NIZK arguments for NP and one-way functions, where \(p\) is a fixed polynomial independent of statement and witness lengths? Formally, either give such a construction or prove an appropriate separation.
status: A 2023 hierarchy proposal by Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs ([A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343)) leaves open a converse gap: SNARGs imply mildly compact witness maps, which in turn imply NIZKs. Ordinary randomized NIZKs do not establish the required output bound.
solved_when: A construction of a deterministic witness map from ordinary NIZK arguments for NP and one-way functions is given whose output set per statement has size at most \(2^{p(\lambda)}\) for a fixed polynomial \(p\) independent of statement and witness lengths; alternatively, a separation showing these primitives do not suffice.
why: It locates the exact assumption strength needed to compress witness diversity without demanding short proofs, resolving the converse gap in the proposed 2023 hierarchy that SNARGs imply mildly compact witness maps, which imply NIZKs.
key_works: Suvradip Chakraborty, Manoj Prabhakaran, Daniel Wichs (2023), [A Map of Witness Maps: New Definitions and Connections](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/343).

title: WE-to-universal-SNARG without short correctness proofs
subfield: Proof-based witness encryption and proof complexity
open: Can the Jin–Kalai–Lombardi–Mathialagan route from witness encryption to a universal SNARG for NP be made to work for arbitrary witness encryption schemes, dropping the requirement that the WE scheme's correctness has a sufficiently short Extended Frege proof, while keeping the explicitly stated auxiliary assumptions on FHE and batch arguments? Alternatively, is there a barrier showing that arbitrary WE cannot yield such universal SNARGs without a proof-friendly subclass?
status: This is a proposed strengthening of the universal-SNARG construction of Zhengzhong Jin, Yael Tauman Kalai, Alex Lombardi, Surya Mathialagan (2025), [Universal SNARGs for NP from Proofs of Correctness](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2015); [DOI 10.1145/3717823.3718104](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718104), whose transparent-CRS nonadaptive universal construction requires WE with a suitably Extended-Frege-friendly correctness proof. Related directions include Extended Frege lower bounds, short proofs of cryptographic correctness, and feasible incompleteness.
solved_when: Either a construction of a universal SNARG from arbitrary WE is given (under the stated FHE and batch-argument assumptions, matching the transparent-CRS nonadaptive universal setting), or a formal separation is established between arbitrary WE and the EF-proof-friendly subclass needed for correctness proofs.
why: It would make a major consequence of witness encryption — universal SNARGs for NP — depend only on the cryptographic functionality of WE, rather than on the proof complexity of proving its correctness.
key_works: Zhengzhong Jin, Yael Tauman Kalai, Alex Lombardi, Surya Mathialagan (2025), [Universal SNARGs for NP from Proofs of Correctness](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2015); [DOI 10.1145/3717823.3718104](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718104).

title: Silent threshold batched IBE without tag-use restrictions
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Can threshold batched IBE be built so that participant keys are generated independently, public aggregation is deterministic, ciphertexts and decryption keys stay compact, and any polynomial number of overlapping release sets is supported — without fixing a bound on the number of releases in setup? In other words, keep all parameters independent of the number of releases, while removing the tag-use restrictions of current silent constructions.
status: The direction is explicit in Gong–Waters–Wee–Wu's May 2026 talk. Silent setup with tag restrictions already exists; later multi-key-per-label work by Guru-Vamsi Policharla (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452), improves reuse but with setup depending on a query bound. Key works: Junqing Gong, Brent Waters, Hoeteck Wee, David J. Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103), [May 2026 slides](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/BatchDecryption0526.pdf).
solved_when: A construction exists with independently generated participant keys, deterministic public aggregation, compact ciphertexts and decryption keys, support for polynomially many overlapping release sets, and no query bound fixed in setup — with parameters independent of the number of releases.
why: It would support changing encrypted transaction pools and release committees without interactive rekeying.
key_works: Junqing Gong, Brent Waters, Hoeteck Wee, David J. Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103), [May 2026 slides](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/BatchDecryption0526.pdf); Guru-Vamsi Policharla (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452).

title: A concrete attack frontier for HLE witness encryption
subfield: Hidden-order witness languages and concrete cryptanalysis
open: How secure is homogeneous-linear-equation witness encryption in practice? Publish reproducible WE challenges that vary the integer-kernel dimension, coefficient size, witness bounds, and hidden-order parameters, and then measure combined lattice and number-theoretic attacks against them, mapping the parameter regions that survive both short-solution and order-recovery attacks at explicitly costed security levels.
status: This is currently a proposed experimental program with no published execution. Bénédikt Tran, Serge Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9) repair earlier small-solution issues and construct extractable HLE-WE using hidden-order and knowledge assumptions; no comparable independent attack frontier was located for this census.
solved_when: A public set of reproducible HLE witness-encryption challenges exists, covering varied integer-kernel dimension, coefficient size, witness bounds, and hidden-order parameters, together with measured results from combined lattice and number-theoretic (order-recovery) attacks identifying parameter regions that resist both attack families at explicitly costed security levels.
why: It would give the first independent, concrete attack frontier for this construction, testing its concrete security before any practical optimization is attempted.
key_works: Bénédikt Tran, Serge Vaudenay (2023), [Extractable Witness Encryption for the Homogeneous Linear Equations Problem](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-41326-1_9).

title: Subquadratic adaptive secret-sharing compilation
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Convert any statically secure computational secret-sharing scheme into an adaptively secure scheme with at most \(O(n\operatorname{polylog}n)\) multiplicative share overhead, preserving the access policy and assumptions. Alternatively, establish a black-box lower bound excluding this target.
status: Quantitative frontier beyond Lu–Waters (2025), whose generic compiler already achieves adaptive security with \(O(n^2)\) overhead.
why: Makes WE-derived access structures usable against adaptive compromise without a quadratic size penalty.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters (2025), [How to Make Any Computational Secret Sharing Scheme Adaptively Secure](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1014).

title: Adaptive succinct sharing without full iO
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Can we build a computational secret-sharing scheme for arbitrary monotone access structures whose shares and public information stay polylogarithmic in the number of parties and remain private even against adaptive corruption — using only witness encryption and LWE rather than indistinguishability obfuscation? Formally, for a monotone circuit \(C\) on \(n\) parties, achieve private shares of \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\) bits and public information of \(n\operatorname{polylog}n+\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|C|)\) bits, counting all per-secret public information, with adaptive privacy.
status: The state of the art is a proposed combination of two narrower advances: Lu–Nassar–Waters achieve \(\lambda\)-bit private shares and \(n+\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|C|)\) public bits from iO and injective OWFs, while Lu–Waters give generic adaptivity with quadratic overhead. Key works: George Lu, Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters (2025/2026), [Succinct Computational Secret Sharing for Monotone Circuits](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/850); Lu–Waters (2025), [How to Make Any Computational Secret Sharing Scheme Adaptively Secure](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1014).
solved_when: A scheme from ordinary witness encryption and LWE exists with adaptive privacy, private shares of \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\) bits, and total public information \(n\operatorname{polylog}n+\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|C|)\) bits (including all per-secret public information).
why: It separates complex authorization policies from the size of their secret shares, giving succinct sharing for rich access structures without relying on full iO.
key_works: George Lu, Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters (2025/2026), [Succinct Computational Secret Sharing for Monotone Circuits](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/850); Lu–Waters (2025), [How to Make Any Computational Secret Sharing Scheme Adaptively Secure](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1014).

title: Monotone-P to monotone-NP sharing completeness
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Determine whether efficient sharing for every monotone polynomial-time access structure implies efficient sharing for all monotone NP access structures through a black-box transformation, allowing explicitly stated OWFs. Give a transformation or oracle separation.
status: Explicitly posed by Komargodski–Naor–Yogev in 2014. Their completeness theorem starts with an NP-complete access structure; recent adaptivity and succinctness compilers do not provide the complexity-class lift.
why: Determines whether efficiently deciding authorization already contains the power to encrypt to arbitrary NP witnesses.
key_works: Ilan Komargodski, Moni Naor, Eylon Yogev (2014/2017), [Secret-Sharing for NP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5698).

title: Perfect-matching access structures from OWFs
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Construct polynomial-size computational secret sharing from OWFs alone when parties represent edges and authorized coalitions contain a perfect matching. Bound private shares, public data, dealer work, and reconstruction work polynomially in graph size and security parameter.
status: Longstanding special-access-structure target. WE plus OWFs gives conditional feasibility, while polynomial-time matching does not itself supply a polynomial-size monotone-circuit implementation.
why: Tests how much obfuscation-like power authorization beyond monotone circuits requires.
key_works: Komargodski–Naor–Yogev (2014/2017), [Secret-Sharing for NP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5698); Amos Beimel (2025), [Secret-Sharing Schemes for General Access Structures: An Introduction](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/518).

title: Upgrade classical-advice EWE to quantum auxiliary states
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: Can a weak extractability (EWE) scheme that is secure against quantum adversaries given classical auxiliary strings be upgraded to security against adversaries holding one copy of an efficiently jointly generated quantum auxiliary state, without strengthening the underlying knowledge assumption? Equivalently, is the classical-advice post-quantum notion strong enough to imply the quantum-auxiliary one?
status: Currently framed as a compiler-or-separation target. Quantum-auxiliary EWE is assumed in 2020–2021 unclonable-decryption constructions, but quantum computation with classical advice does not establish that premise. Related lines include BQP/poly versus BQP/qpoly and constructive reductions with non-reproducible advice (WE-059, WE-097); key work: Marios Georgiou, Mark Zhandry (2020), [Unclonable Decryption Keys](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/877).
solved_when: Either a compiler is exhibited that converts any classically-advice-secure post-quantum EWE scheme into one secure with a single copy of a jointly generated quantum auxiliary state (under the same knowledge assumption), or a separation is shown — a scheme secure in the classical-advice model that fails in the quantum-auxiliary model.
why: Quantum-token applications of classical witness extraction, such as unclonable decryption, actually assume the quantum-auxiliary premise, so resolving this determines whether those constructions can rest on the weaker, more justifiable classical-advice security notion.
key_works: Marios Georgiou, Mark Zhandry (2020), [Unclonable Decryption Keys](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/877).

title: Constructive adaptive reductions from quantum WE distinguishers
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: For adaptive classical reductions whose solution spaces have polynomial size, when can a quantum compiler reuse only the original auxiliary state — with polynomial overhead and no resampling oracle — while preserving the reduction's guarantees? Give either such a compiler or a separation for a specified class of adaptive reductions.
status: This is a proposed witness-encryption-specific extension beyond Nir Bitansky, Zvika Brakerski, Yael Tauman Kalai (2022), [Constructive Post-Quantum Reductions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02314), whose theorem covers only the nonadaptive setting. Known obstructions for superpolynomial-size solution spaces rule out any unrestricted conversion claim.
solved_when: Either a compiler is exhibited that converts adaptive reductions with polynomial-size solution spaces using only the original auxiliary state, polynomial overhead, and no resampling oracle; or a separation is proved showing such a conversion is impossible for a specified reduction class.
why: It turns successful quantum distinguishers against witness encryption into actual attacks on the underlying assumption by constructively extracting witnesses, closing the gap between distinguishing and breaking.
key_works: Nir Bitansky, Zvika Brakerski, Yael Tauman Kalai (2022), [Constructive Post-Quantum Reductions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02314).

title: Extraction without inverse access to a quantum decryptor
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: When a witness-encryption relation is accessed only through forward queries to a stateful quantum decryptor, which relations still admit extraction? A satisfactory answer would characterize the relations for which extraction is possible, prove query lower bounds where it is not, or identify what additional interfaces would restore extractability.
status: The problem is currently a proposed interface boundary motivated by quantum rewinding techniques and oracle separations; related threads include quantum query lower bounds, black-box process inversion, and items WE-062 and WE-252. Key work: Andris Ambainis, Ansis Rosmanis, Dominique Unruh (2014), [Quantum Attacks on Classical Proof Systems — The Hardness of Quantum Rewinding](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6898).
solved_when: A characterization exists of the witness-encryption relations permitting extraction from forward-only access to a stateful quantum decryptor, together with proven query lower bounds or a specification of the additional interfaces required when inverse-unitary access is unavailable.
why: It separates formal knowledge claims from information that can actually be recovered from an externally operated device, delimiting what constructive reductions can achieve without inverse access.
key_works: Andris Ambainis, Ansis Rosmanis, Dominique Unruh (2014), [Quantum Attacks on Classical Proof Systems — The Hardness of Quantum Rewinding](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6898).

title: Prove the needed coset-verifier evasive composability
subfield: Quantum-safe knowledge assumptions for lattice and obfuscation routes
open: Can the coset-authenticated states and the differently based ZX-verifier obfuscations used in quantum arguments of knowledge be shown jointly hiding, using only ordinary post-quantum indistinguishability obfuscation, without assuming a separate evasive-composability heuristic? Formally, prove the needed coset-verifier evasive composability from post-quantum iO alone.
status: This is an explicit 2025/2026 open proof step. The unrestricted heuristic has self-referential counterexamples; the construction needs structured samplers. Key work: James Bartusek, Ruta Jawale, Justin Raizes, Kabir Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).
solved_when: A proof of joint hiding for the particular coset-authenticated states and differently based ZX-verifier obfuscations is given, deriving it from ordinary post-quantum iO rather than an additional evasive-composability heuristic (e.g., via structured samplers).
why: It strengthens the quantum proof infrastructure from which QMA condition encryption may be compiled.
key_works: James Bartusek, Ruta Jawale, Justin Raizes, Kabir Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Near-perfect extraction for a fixed quantum verifier
subfield: Extractable QMA conditions and witness representation
open: Can a witness accepted with probability \(1-\operatorname{negl}(\lambda)\) by the advertised strongly complete verifier — the same verifier, not an amplified replacement — be extracted in polynomial time and without extra input-witness copies? Alternatively, a tight barrier proof in a restricted model would settle the question from the other side.
status: This is a proposed quality frontier beyond acceptance \(1-\gamma\) for arbitrarily small inverse-polynomial \(\gamma\); note that replacing the verifier with an amplified one changes the target. Related work: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).
solved_when: Either a polynomial-time extractor for the same advertised strongly complete verifier outputs a witness from a \(1-\operatorname{negl}(\lambda)\) acceptance using no extra input-witness copies, or a tight impossibility is proven in a suitably restricted model.
why: It bounds the failure probability in settings where a single scarce extracted witness unlocks many independently issued ciphertexts, so extraction quality directly controls security there.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Condition encryption with a quantum instance
subfield: Extractable QMA conditions and witness representation
open: Can we build witness encryption whose public condition is not just a classical description but includes a bounded number of copies of an unknown quantum specimen? More precisely, construct a nonvacuous witness-encryption scheme whose condition takes such quantum instances, with the encryption procedure and the notion of witness validity defined relative to the received specimen.
status: The model has been proposed as going beyond QMA-WE, whose conditions are given only by classical instance descriptions; proofs concerning received quantum states already exist, notably in Léo Colisson, Frédéric Grosshans, Elham Kashefi (2025), [Non-Interactive and Non-Destructive Zero-Knowledge Proofs on Quantum States and Multi-Party Generation of Authorized Hidden GHZ States](https://doi.org/10.1145/3721487).
solved_when: A witness-encryption scheme is constructed whose public condition contains bounded copies of an unknown quantum state, together with a specification of how encryption consumes the specimen and which witnesses count as valid relative to it; the construction must be nonvacuous (not trivially satisfiable or decryptable).
why: It would let cryptographic conditions be tied to actual physical quantum resources that have no classical circuit description, extending witness encryption to settings where the instance itself is a quantum state.
key_works: Léo Colisson, Frédéric Grosshans, Elham Kashefi (2025), [Non-Interactive and Non-Destructive Zero-Knowledge Proofs on Quantum States and Multi-Party Generation of Authorized Hidden GHZ States](https://doi.org/10.1145/3721487).

title: State-bound confidential firmware rollout
subfield: Software provenance and confidential deployment
open: Can we release firmware decryption keys only to devices that are in a genuinely authorized state, without any per-device interaction with the distributor, so that rollback protection survives interrupted installations, recovery, and supplier-key compromise?
status: A 10×-tier lifecycle target has been proposed. Uptane (Kuppusamy et al. (2016), [Uptane: Securing Software Updates for Automobiles](https://uptane.org/papers/kuppusamy_escar_16.pdf)) provides secure-update foundations, but witness encryption does not itself certify live device state or successful installation.
solved_when: A deployment scheme meets the 10×-tier lifecycle target: keys are released only to authorized device states, rollback protection is preserved through interrupted installation, recovery, and supplier-key compromise, and no per-device sender interaction is required.
why: It enables confidential, staged firmware distribution to intermittently connected fleets, which current secure-update foundations cannot do.
key_works: Kuppusamy et al. (2016), [Uptane: Securing Software Updates for Automobiles](https://uptane.org/papers/kuppusamy_escar_16.pdf).

title: Security-parameter-sized prime fields
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can the prime field used in the generic-group witness-encryption construction be shrunk to about λ + log n bits, so that field arithmetic costs essentially the security parameter rather than more? Formally, is there a variant of the construction whose prime-field bit length is O(λ + log n) while preserving the rank gap and the accompanying security analysis?
status: The current state of the art is the 2026 generic-group construction of Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275); reducing the required bit length is a proposed quantitative refinement of that construction.
solved_when: A variant of the 2026 generic-group construction is given whose prime-field bit length is O(λ + log n), with the rank gap and security analysis preserved.
why: The field size directly controls arithmetic, encoding, and ciphertext costs, so a smaller prime field yields cheaper witness encryption.
key_works: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).
aliases: Small-bitlength field WE; this does not mean polynomial-order cryptographic groups.

title: Tight generic-group witness extraction
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: How fast, and with what success probability, can a witness be extracted from an adversary interacting with a generic group, when the extractor's resources are measured against the adversary's advantage, query count, and witness size? A satisfying answer gives tight — not merely polynomial-time — extraction bounds as explicit functions of these parameters.
status: A polynomial-time extraction claim from October 2026 established the current frontier; the open question is the quantitative frontier beyond it. Key works: Campanelli (2026), [A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399); Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).
solved_when: Extractor time and success probability are characterized as optimal functions of adversarial advantage, query count, and witness size, improving on October 2026's polynomial-time extraction claim.
why: It converts existential extractability into concrete, quantitative guarantees that applications can rely on.
key_works: Campanelli (2026), [A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399); Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).

title: Remove random-access help in learning-based WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can the learning-to-witness-encryption implication be established when the learner has only ordinary sample access to the distribution? In other words, can the random-access help that the current characterization relies on be removed?
status: An explicit frontier arising from the 2025 learning connection of Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).
solved_when: The implication from learning hardness to witness encryption is proved for a learner with standard sample access alone, with no additional random-access (query) help.
why: It would align the characterization with the standard interfaces of learning theory, making the meta-complexity connection meaningful for ordinary PAC-style sample complexity rather than an augmented query model.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Eliminate the half-Levin witness-map requirement
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can the implication from learning hardness to witness encryption (WE) be recovered from weaker reductions — ones that do not explicitly map satisfying assignments into the required learning witnesses? Formally, this asks whether the current "half-Levin" witness-map requirement in the reduction can be removed.
status: Currently a proposed strengthening of the 2025 reduction framework of Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).
solved_when: A reduction framework is exhibited that derives WE from learning hardness without requiring the reduction to explicitly map satisfying assignments to learning witnesses, recovering the learning-to-WE implication.
why: It would make the existing NP-hardness reductions potentially usable for constructing witness encryption, rather than requiring bespoke witness-preserving reductions.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Sublinear indexed positional WE without added LWE
subfield: Offline, batched, positional, and signature-based WE
open: Can witness encryption be made positional and indexed-succinct from plain witness encryption alone? Formally, is there an N^ε-succinct indexed positional witness encryption scheme whose security rests on no assumption beyond plain WE?
status: The 2026 result of Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932), establishes an indexed N^ε-succinct construction under combined assumptions; O(N) constructions do not solve this target.
solved_when: An indexed positional witness encryption scheme with N^ε-succinctness is constructed and proved secure using only plain witness encryption, with no additional LWE (or other) premise.
why: It clarifies exactly how much extra power is required to make witness encryption positional, separating what plain WE can achieve from what needs stronger assumptions.
key_works: Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Private catch-up for dormant registered receivers
subfield: Permissionless registration and encrypted directories
open: Can a registered encrypted directory let a long-dormant receiver catch up on everything it missed — privately, and without communication or server cost that grows with the number of missed registrations? Formally, the goal is a catch-up mechanism with polylogarithmic communication and amortized server work, while retaining polylogarithmic registration-update work and publicly verifiable helper correctness.
status: The problem is currently framed as a 1,000×-tier target beyond existing helper-update functionality, building on Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812); related directions include private information retrieval, authenticated dynamic data structures, intermittent-client synchronization, and WE-086.
solved_when: A construction achieves the 1,000×-tier target beyond existing helper-update functionality, with catch-up communication and amortized server work polylogarithmic and independent of the number of missed registrations, polylogarithmic registration-update work, and publicly verifiable helper correctness.
why: It makes encrypted directories usable by intermittently connected devices, instead of hiding a linear server scan behind the interface.
key_works: Freitag–Waters–Wu (2023/2025), [How to Use (Plain) Witness Encryption: Registered ABE, Flexible Broadcast, and More](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/812).

title: Fully succinct positional WE from ordinary WE and LWE
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Can we build a positional witness encryption scheme that compares the entire witness against a secret cutoff, using only ordinary NP witness encryption and LWE, so that ciphertexts stay polynomial in the verifier size, security parameter, and witness length? Equivalently, can indexed positional witness encryption be achieved with only polylogarithmic dependence on the size of the index space?
status: The frontier was sharpened by Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), whose construction achieves \(N^\varepsilon\) dependence for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) but compares a separate index rather than the full witness.
solved_when: A construction is given, from ordinary NP witness encryption and LWE, achieving ciphertext size polynomial in verifier size, security parameter, and witness length (equivalently, polylogarithmic dependence on index-space size), with the ciphertext comparing the full witness against the secret cutoff.
why: It would support exponentially large ordered witness spaces without incurring exponential ciphertext growth.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932); [full version](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Rate-one null obfuscation below full iO
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Can null-input-indistinguishability obfuscation be realized with only additive size overhead — so that nesting obfuscations composes circuit sizes additively rather than multiplicatively — starting from just standard witness encryption plus LWE? Alternatively, a separation showing this rate demands substantially stronger primitives would equally resolve the question.
status: Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026) identify rate-one null-iO below full iO as a missing ingredient; the specific WE-plus-LWE target is proposed here. Key work: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).
solved_when: A construction of null-iO from ordinary witness encryption and LWE is given whose obfuscation size is the original circuit size plus an additive overhead, or a proof is given that rate-one null-iO requires substantially stronger primitives than WE plus LWE.
why: It would make deep recursive encryption compilers plausible in practice, and it isolates whether succinctness itself raises the assumption strength needed for null obfuscation.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/Cutoff-iO.pdf).

title: Polylogarithmic ciphertexts for publicly traceable registered broadcast
subfield: Positional witness encryption and obfuscation succinctness
open: Can we build a registered broadcast-and-trace scheme with public tracing and full collusion resistance whose ciphertext overhead shrinks to polynomial in the security parameter and \(\log N\), starting only from ordinary witness encryption plus LWE? Recipient-set descriptions are counted separately, and the existing registration semantics must be retained.
status: The target is a parameter improvement beyond the \(N^\varepsilon\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) ciphertext bound of Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026) [Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), "Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional," https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932]; full collusion resistance is already achieved, and the missing improvement concerns ciphertext size.
solved_when: A construction from ordinary WE plus LWE achieves registered broadcast-and-trace with public tracing, full collusion resistance, and ciphertext overhead polynomial in \(\lambda\) and \(\log N\) (with recipient-set descriptions counted separately and the existing registration semantics preserved), improving on the \(N^\varepsilon\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bound.
why: It enables publicly accountable distribution with independently generated subscriber keys at very large population sizes.
key_works: Shafik Nassar, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Replace the quantum pseudorandom oracle
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Obtain the QMA-WE consequences of the quantum-pseudorandom-oracle model in the ordinary quantum random-oracle model, or separate the models for this task.
status: The 2025/2026 route uses QPrO; hidden-handle pseudorandom oracles are not ordinary random oracles.
why: Removes a consequential idealization from the construction route.
key_works: Bartusek–Jawale–Raizes–Tomer (2025/2026), [A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05316).

title: Oracle separation of QMA from QCIP[2]
subfield: Post-quantum classical WE and quantum-witness encryption
open: Is there an oracle relative to which QMA is not contained in QCIP[2], two-message classical-channel quantum interactive proofs? Ideally the oracle should be classical.
status: This is an explicit next step for 2026; separating QMA from QCMA alone is known to be insufficient. Key work: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), [Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25195).
solved_when: An oracle — classical if possible — is exhibited relative to which QMA ⊄ QCIP[2].
why: It supplies structural evidence for the gap underlying the barriers facing QMA witness encryption.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), [Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25195).

title: Negligible-disturbance extraction for a live quantum escrow
subfield: Quantum extractability: auxiliary states and constructive reductions
open: Can we extract a witness from a quantum adversary for witness encryption of unique-witness NP relations while disturbing its state so little that, jointly with an entangled reference held by an outsider, the simulation error is negligible — and still do it in polynomial time?
status: Currently a proposed composition target: extraction with an adjustable inverse-polynomial simulation error is established, but pushing to negligible error can force superpolynomial runtime. Key work: Nai-Hui Chia, Kai-Min Chung, Xiao Liang, Takashi Yamakawa (2022), [Post-Quantum Simulatable Extraction with Minimal Assumptions: Black-Box and Constant-Round](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08665).
solved_when: An extractor exists that, for unique-witness NP relations, extracts from quantum EWE adversaries, simulates the residual state jointly with an inaccessible entangled reference to negligible error, and runs in polynomial time.
why: It would let a party interact further with the escrow (or the adversary) without silently swapping out its quantum state, enabling composable state restoration in subsequent escrow interactions.
key_works: Nai-Hui Chia, Kai-Min Chung, Xiao Liang, Takashi Yamakawa (2022), [Post-Quantum Simulatable Extraction with Minimal Assumptions: Black-Box and Constant-Round](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08665).

title: A single-copy quantum laconic characterization
subfield: Quantum language classes and witness resources
open: Can QMA witness encryption be characterized through laconic zero-knowledge proofs using only a single copy of the quantum witness? Equivalently, either establish a quantum analogue of the known classical equivalence under a one-copy witness budget, or prove that the classical transformation intrinsically requires additional witness copies.
status: The problem is a proposed quantum analogue of the 2026 classical equivalence. Key works include Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/); and Kalai–Khurana–Raizes (2026), [How to Classically Verify a Quantum Cat without Killing It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09282). Related themes include no-cloning and witness-preserving verification.
solved_when: Either a proof that QMA-WE admits a laconic characterization with a one-copy quantum-witness budget, or a proof that any such transformation intrinsically needs more than one copy of the witness.
why: A solution determines which witness-encryption transformations are physically realizable: those assuming witness duplication violate no-cloning and cannot be executed on quantum witnesses.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/); Kalai–Khurana–Raizes (2026), [How to Classically Verify a Quantum Cat without Killing It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09282).

title: Sublinear setup for black-box pairing registered ABE
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can registered attribute-based encryption for monotone span programs be realized with a structured common reference string of sublinear size in the number of users? The goal is a construction using only black-box pairing operations and compact aggregated keys, with every reusable public table counted toward setup — or, failing that, a lower bound in a specified algebraic model.
status: The sublinear-CRS question appears in Wu’s 2024 research agenda (David J. Wu (2024), [Registration-Based Cryptography](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/RegistrationCrypto0524.pdf)). Linear setup for general monotone policies was achieved in 2026 by Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf); sublinear setup remains distinct and open.
solved_when: A construction is given with a structured CRS of \(o(N)\) group elements for registered ABE supporting monotone span programs, using black-box pairing operations and compact aggregated keys, counting all reusable public tables as setup; or a lower bound is proven in a specified algebraic model showing this impossible.
why: It would reduce population-dependent deployment costs without invoking general-purpose witness encryption or obfuscation, keeping registered ABE deployable as policies and user bases grow.
key_works: David J.
