Wu (2024), [Registration-Based Cryptography](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/talks/RegistrationCrypto0524.pdf); Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Sublinear individual keys with linear registration setup
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can each user's public key in black-box pairing registered ABE be made sublinear — \(o(N)\) group elements — while keeping the CRS at \(O(N)\), supporting general monotone policies, and maintaining compact master/helper keys, without the saving being shifted into per-user public auxiliary data?
status: Proposed quantitative target; no construction achieves it yet. The 2026 linear-CRS construction of Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf), retains linear individual public keys.
solved_when: A construction achieves individual public keys of \(o(N)\) group elements together with an \(O(N)\) CRS, general monotone policies, and compact master/helper keys, with no compensating growth in per-user public auxiliary data.
why: It removes quadratic aggregate upload and storage across a population of \(N\) users.
key_works: Roy Stracovsky, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Linear-CRS pairing registration across independent authorities
subfield: Registered encryption and decentralized policy languages
open: Can a pairing-based multi-authority registered attribute-based encryption scheme support a common reference string whose size grows only linearly in the supported population, while still admitting monotone span-program policies and curators who operate independently without coordination? Any additional dependence on the number of authorities and the attribute-universe size should be stated explicitly.
status: The target was proposed following a 2025 multi-authority construction, George Lu, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2025), [Multi-Authority Registered Attribute-Based Encryption](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredMA-ABE.pdf), and a 2026 single-authority linear-CRS result, Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf); neither establishes the combined guarantee.
solved_when: A construction is given achieving a CRS linear in the supported population for pairing-based multi-authority registered ABE that preserves monotone span-program policies and independent, non-coordinating curators, with any extra dependence on authority count and attribute-universe size made explicit.
why: It makes federated conditional encryption substantially cheaper to initialize and maintain across independently run domains.
key_works: George Lu, Brent Waters, David J. Wu (2025), [Multi-Authority Registered Attribute-Based Encryption](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredMA-ABE.pdf); Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dwu4/papers/RegisteredABE-Linear.pdf).

title: Sublinear pairing parameters for batched IBE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Can pairing-based batched identity-based encryption be built so that the public parameters contain only \(o(B)\) group elements, where \(B\) is the maximum batch size, while keeping ciphertexts and batch decryption keys of constant size? Alternatively, if setup must scale linearly with \(B\), establish a lower bound showing this in the relevant algebraic model.
status: An explicit direction as of May 2026. The partial-fraction construction of Dan Boneh, Rohit Nema, Arnab Roy, Ertem Nusret Tas (2026), [Efficient Batch Threshold Encryption Using Partial Fraction Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/674) still has linear public parameters. Related prior work includes Gong–Waters–Wee–Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103).
solved_when: A construction (or lower bound) is given: either a pairing-based batched IBE scheme with \(o(B)\) public-parameter group elements for maximum batch size \(B\) that retains constant-size ciphertexts and constant-size batch decryption keys, or a proof that linear-size setup is necessary in the specified algebraic model.
why: It would allow large future release sets without setup costs proportional to their maximum size, removing a linear bottleneck in deploying batched IBE at scale.
key_works: Gong–Waters–Wee–Wu (2026), [Threshold Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Pairings in the Plain Model](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2103); Dan Boneh, Rohit Nema, Arnab Roy, Ertem Nusret Tas (2026), [Efficient Batch Threshold Encryption Using Partial Fraction Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/674).

title: Additive setup cost for multi-key batched IBE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Can batched identity-based encryption support \(q\) decryption-key queries per label and batch size \(B\) with a common reference string of size \(\widetilde O(B+q)\) rather than \(O(qB)\), while keeping ciphertexts constant-size and release keys compact? The target additionally requires security against adversarially chosen release sets that overlap.
status: This is a proposed quantitative target following Guru-Vamsi Polichitra (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452), which established multi-key-per-label feasibility with an \(O(qB)\) CRS.
solved_when: A construction achieves CRS size \(\widetilde O(B+q)\) (additive rather than multiplicative in \(q\) and \(B\)), supports \(q\) decryption-key queries per label and batches of size \(B\), retains constant-size ciphertexts and compact release keys, and is proven secure for overlapping adversarially chosen release sets.
why: Without additive setup cost, each repeated release multiplies the setup burden; achieving it prevents the setup from growing as \(O(qB)\).
key_works: Guru-Vamsi Policharla (2026), [Labeled Multi-Key Batched IBE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1452).

title: Compact batched IBE from plain LWE
subfield: Signature languages, batched IBE, and compact conditional release
open: Can batched identity-based encryption be built in the standard model from plain LWE, rather than succinct LWE, while keeping master public keys, ciphertexts, and batch keys polynomial in the security parameter \(\lambda\) and \(\log B\)? A full answer should also specify the required modulus-to-noise ratio.
status: This is a proposed assumption-reduction target following Saisi Xiong, Yijian Zhang, Jie Chen (2026), [Efficient Batched IBE from Lattices in the Standard Model](https://cic.iacr.org/p/3/2/18); [DOI 10.62056/aksude-3](https://doi.org/10.62056/aksude-3), which achieves standard-model lattice batched IBE from succinct LWE using compact inner-product encryption with decomposable key generation.
solved_when: A standard-model batched IBE scheme is constructed from plain LWE whose master public keys, ciphertexts, and batch keys are all polynomial in \(\lambda\) and \(\log B\), with an explicit statement of the required modulus-to-noise ratio.
why: It would give quantum-resistant bulk conditional release a special-language route independent of general NP witness encryption.
key_works: Saisi Xiong, Yijian Zhang, Jie Chen (2026), [Efficient Batched IBE from Lattices in the Standard Model](https://cic.iacr.org/p/3/2/18); [DOI 10.62056/aksude-3](https://doi.org/10.62056/aksude-3).

title: Adaptive evolving mNP sharing with short immutable shares
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Can we build, from ordinary witness encryption plus LWE, a secret-sharing scheme that remains adaptively private for any rigid, efficiently described evolving monotone-NP access structure, without knowing the final population or how the policy will evolve? Formally, old shares must stay immutable, each new share must be \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n,\log|V_n|)\) bits, and the cumulative per-secret public payload must be \(O(n\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|V_n|))\), even while arrivals and corruptions interleave.
status: Proposed as a strengthening of Francati–Giammusso–Venturi (2025/2026). Evolving mNP sharing and adaptive evolving monotone-circuit sharing exist; the succinctness inherited from succinct witness encryption does not establish these bounds from ordinary WE.
solved_when: A construction from ordinary WE plus LWE achieves adaptive privacy for all rigid, efficiently described evolving mNP policies with unknown final population and future evolution, immutable old shares, individual new shares of \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n,\log|V_n|)\) bits, and cumulative per-secret public payload \(O(n\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log|V_n|))\) under interleaved arrivals and corruptions.
why: It would let institutions accept new participants for decades without recalling or reissuing all existing shares.
key_works: Danilo Francati, Sara Giammusso, Daniele Venturi (2025/2026), [Taming Adaptive Security and New Access Structures in Evolving Secret Sharing](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-95-5125-5_3).

title: Succinct traceable sharing for witness access structures
subfield: Witness encryption and computational secret sharing
open: Can we give a traceable secret-sharing scheme for general witness access structures whose shares and public data remain succinct? Specifically, the goal is succinct mNP sharing with black-box tracing that cannot frame honest participants, where private shares are \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\) bits, public data is near-linear in size, and a succinct verifier term is included — all under a nonvacuous general-access tracing game.
status: The current state of the art is the corrected constructions and security tradeoffs of Goyal–Jain–Partap, whose work shows that earlier tracing definitions can become vacuous for general access structures; this problem proposes a quantitative target beyond those constructions. Key works: Vipul Goyal, Abhishek Jain, Aditi Partap (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Revisited](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1980); Oriol Farràs, Miquel Guiot (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Schemes for General Access Structures](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1120).
solved_when: A construction exists achieving non-frameable black-box tracing for succinct mNP sharing with \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,\log n)\)-bit private shares and near-linear public data plus a succinct verifier term, with security proven via a nonvacuous general-access tracing game covering unauthorized stored and supplementary coalitions whose union is authorized, with explicit query distributions and success thresholds.
why: It would make private conditional decryption authority accountable when participants sell reconstruction services, so leaking or commercializing decryption ability can be traced back to the responsible set of shareholders.
key_works: Vipul Goyal, Abhishek Jain, Aditi Partap (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Revisited](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1980); Oriol Farràs, Miquel Guiot (2025/2026), [Traceable Secret Sharing Schemes for General Access Structures](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1120).

title: Plain-to-extractable WE for controlled instance distributions
subfield: General assumptions and reductions
open: Can extractable witness encryption be built from plain witness encryption alone, when instances are drawn independently from hard NP-search distributions? The formal target is a compiler that handles instance-independent adversarial advice and grants the extractor explicit access, without introducing any knowledge-type assumption.
status: This is a proposed compiler frontier. It is known that false-instance security gives no generic hard-true guarantee, and unrestricted auxiliary input encounters conditional barriers, as shown by Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility) exists for independently sampled hard NP-search instance distributions, providing extractable security against adversaries with instance-independent auxiliary input and an explicitly specified extractor, under plain WE with no added knowledge assumption.
why: A positive answer would justify theorem and event rewards under weaker premises than currently needed.
key_works: Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).

title: Separate ordinary WE from general obfuscation
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Is general witness encryption strictly weaker than indistinguishability obfuscation, in the sense that no arbitrary construction can build iO from WE alone — or, conversely, can iO be derived from WE together with explicitly identified weaker primitives?
status: Open since 2013. Black-box barriers and 2026 indexed positional-WE results do not settle arbitrary reductions. Key works: Garg–Mahmoody–Mohammed (2017), [Lower Bounds on Obfuscation from All-or-Nothing Encryption Primitives](https://momahmoody.github.io/files/papers/IO-all-or-nothing.pdf); Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).
solved_when: A proof that general WE is strictly weaker than iO under arbitrary constructions, or an explicit construction of iO from WE plus identified weaker primitives.
why: It determines whether condition encryption inherits the full difficulty of program obfuscation, or constitutes a genuinely weaker cryptographic object.
key_works: Garg–Mahmoody–Mohammed (2017), [Lower Bounds on Obfuscation from All-or-Nothing Encryption Primitives](https://momahmoody.github.io/files/papers/IO-all-or-nothing.pdf); Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs: Making Witness Encryption Positional](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: Statistical WE versus smooth projective hashing
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Determine whether every statistically secure WE relation admits a comparably efficient smooth projective hash system, or exhibit a separating relation.
status: Projective hashing supplies one direction; the 2026 laconic characterization provides a different proof-system perspective.
why: Identifies whether projective hashing exhausts useful information-theoretic witness encryption.
key_works: Cramer–Shoup (2002), [Universal Hash Proofs and a Paradigm for Adaptive Chosen Ciphertext Secure Public-Key Encryption](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-46035-7_4); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Statistical WE throughout efficiently witnessed SZK
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: Which languages in NP∩SZK admit witness encryption whose ciphertexts are statistically hidden, yet decryption succeeds efficiently using the designated NP witness? A complete characterization would delimit statistical witness encryption inside the efficiently witnessed portion of SZK.
status: The state of the art is the established characterization via laconic special-honest-verifier statistical zero knowledge; the proposed classification would go beyond this. Key works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).
solved_when: A full characterization exists of the languages in NP∩SZK that admit statistical witness encryption with efficient decryption from their designated NP witnesses.
why: It identifies the precise conditions under which ciphertext secrecy survives unlimited adversarial computation, sharpening our map of statistical security for witness encryption.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: The superlogarithmic laconicity boundary
subfield: Foundations: language expressivity and equivalences
open: How much communication must a laconic prover be allowed before witness encryption can no longer be built efficiently from it? Formally, determine the greatest prover-communication bound from which efficient witness encryption follows, or prove a threshold separating logarithmic from superlogarithmic protocols.
status: This boundary question was proposed after the 2026 characterization; direct transcript enumeration becomes superpolynomial beyond logarithmic communication. Key work: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).
solved_when: Either a superlogarithmic prover-communication bound is identified from which efficient witness encryption still follows, or a threshold is proven separating logarithmic from superlogarithmic protocols.
why: It clarifies whether slightly longer arguments remain sufficient for witness encryption, pinning down the fine-grained communication boundary of the construction.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/revision/1/download).

title: Unconditional half-Levin NP-hardness of improper learning
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can the NP-hardness of improper learning be established unconditionally, via witness-preserving half-Levin reductions, without assuming the existence of witness encryption?
status: The 2025 characterization of Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34), identifies a strong connection between witness encryption and learning hardness; unconditional hardness would provide the corresponding cryptographic consequences.
solved_when: A proof of NP-hardness of improper learning is obtained through witness-preserving half-Levin reductions with no assumption of witness encryption (WE).
why: It converts a learning-theoretic hardness theorem into a route toward conditional encryption, yielding cryptographic consequences from unconditional hardness.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Unconditional WE against restricted adversaries
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can we build a witness encryption scheme, with no unproven assumptions, that is provably secure against some explicit restricted class of adversaries? Formally, construct a meaningful WE scheme whose security against a specified restricted adversary class follows unconditionally from circuit lower bounds or learning-theoretic lower bounds, with the restriction chosen so that both decryption and security remain nontrivial problems.
status: Identified as a research direction in 2025; the key constraint recognized so far is that the adversary restriction must leave a nontrivial decryption and security problem. The direction is connected to Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34), and to circuit lower bounds, bounded-depth cryptography, and restricted learning.
solved_when: An explicit witness encryption scheme is constructed whose security against a named restricted adversary class is proven unconditionally via circuit or learning lower bounds, where the restriction still leaves a nontrivial decryption task and a nontrivial security question.
why: Such a construction would yield unconditional prototypes of witness encryption and expose which computational hardness actually powers WE, grounding its security in circuit and learning lower bounds rather than unproven assumptions.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Uniform-example-distribution learning characterization
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Is worst-case hardness of witness encryption (WE) already characterized by learning hardness under a single fixed uniform example distribution, or does the known equivalence genuinely require more general distributions? Formally: characterize WE via learning hardness for the uniform distribution alone, or isolate which more general distributions are necessary.
status: The question arises as a proposed restriction of the 2025 equivalence of Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A characterization of WE in terms of learning hardness under a fixed uniform example distribution is established, or a proof that the equivalence provably fails for uniform distributions alone, thereby isolating the necessity of more general distributions.
why: It would tie witness encryption directly to central distribution-specific learning problems, such as uniform-distribution learning, pseudorandom restrictions, and distributional complexity.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Uniform versus nonuniform WE power
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Which implications of witness encryption survive when both security and reductions are restricted to uniform algorithms, and where do the uniform and nonuniform formulations of WE power provably separate?
status: The 2025 learning results — Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34) — expose consequential nonuniformity requirements; related lines include BPP versus P/poly and uniform hardness amplification.
solved_when: The uniform-versus-nonuniform landscape for WE-based implications is settled: each known implication is either carried over with uniform security and uniform reductions or shown to fail under such restrictions, with an explicit separation where uniform and nonuniform formulations differ.
why: It prevents advice assumptions from silently strengthening cryptographic conclusions, so results stated for uniform algorithms are not unwittingly leaning on nonuniform power.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: Cryptographic consequences of uniform-only WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: What cryptographic consequences can be derived from witness encryption that is secure only against uniform attackers, assuming explicit uniform complexity assumptions? In other words, establish the strongest encryption and one-wayness conclusions obtainable in the uniform-only setting.
status: A proposed clarification; existing results differ in their treatment of uniformity, all-input security, and hardness premises. Key works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download).
solved_when: A characterization is established of the encryption and one-wayness primitives implied by uniform-only WE under explicit uniform assumptions, clarifying which consequences hold and which do not.
why: It separates the computational assumptions genuinely necessary for these consequences from artifacts of the proofs, sharpening the foundations connecting witness encryption, one-way functions, and average-case complexity.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2025), [A Note on Zero-Knowledge for NP and One-Way Functions](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/095/revision/2/download).

title: Remove auxiliary circuit hardness from short-WE consequences
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can the known connection between short witness encryption and GapDistMCSP be established purely from succinct witness encryption, without assuming hardness of exponential-time computation against circuits? More precisely, derive the short-WE/GapDistMCSP relationship while eliminating the auxiliary circuit-hardness assumption.
status: Currently a proposed assumption-removal target in the 2025 meta-complexity connection, drawing on Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); related directions include GapDistMCSP, derandomization, and exponential circuit lower bounds.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the short-WE/GapDistMCSP relationship that uses no additional assumption about exponential-time hardness against circuits.
why: It isolates whether succinct witness encryption alone explains the resulting hardness, separating the intrinsic strength of short WE from borrowed circuit lower bounds.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: A WE-only barrier to Levin hardness of GapMCSP
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: What is the weakest witness-encryption premise that suffices to rule out appropriate Levin reductions establishing NP-hardness of GapMCSP? More precisely, can the barrier be isolated so that the only additional hypothesis beyond the reduction framework itself is a minimally strong form of witness encryption?
status: Existing meta-complexity barriers, notably Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36), and Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34), rely on particular cryptographic or reduction hypotheses; removing these additional premises remains the target.
solved_when: A witness-encryption assumption is identified that provably obstructs appropriate Levin reductions from proving NP-hardness of GapMCSP, with no additional cryptographic or reduction hypotheses assumed beyond that WE premise.
why: It would explain why natural completeness strategies for GapMCSP may inherently fail, clarifying whether witness encryption alone is the source of the obstruction.
key_works: Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36); Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: WE-induced barriers for learning reductions
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Which kinds of learning reductions — witness-preserving, randomized, adaptive, or oracle — are incompatible with specified forms of witness encryption? A formal classification would delineate exactly which reduction types cannot coexist with the assumed WE primitives.
status: Proposed as an extension of the 2024–2025 meta-complexity and learning barriers, building on Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34) and Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36).
solved_when: A classification is given of the reduction types (witness-preserving, randomized, adaptive, and oracle learning reductions) that are incompatible with the specified forms of witness encryption, separating viable from impossible reductions.
why: It tells learning-hardness researchers which reduction types remain viable, so effort is not spent on approaches that WE provably blocks.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34); Mazor–Pass (2024), [CCC 2024 paper](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.36).

title: Polynomial-security WE for strong conditional-Kolmogorov hardness
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can polynomially secure witness encryption yield the strongest known approximation-hardness results for time-bounded conditional Kolmogorov complexity? Formally, does WE with only polynomial security suffice to derive these hardness consequences for Kᵗ(x|y)?
status: Proposed as a weakening of cryptographic hardness requirements in the 2023/2025 line of work (Huang–Ilange–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483)); related topics include approximation of Kᵗ(x|y) and fine-grained cryptography.
solved_when: A proof establishes the strongest known approximation-hardness consequences for time-bounded conditional Kolmogorov complexity assuming only polynomially secure witness encryption.
why: It would connect conventional cryptographic security levels to quantitative meta-complexity, weakening the hardness assumptions needed for these consequences.
key_works: Huang–Ilango–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483).

title: Near-input-length time bounds for conditional description hardness
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can the hardness of approximating conditional Kolmogorov complexity derived from witness encryption be pushed to time bounds close to the input length itself, while still keeping a meaningful approximation gap?
status: The current frontier is quantitative: the achievable time bounds and the reduction's overhead remain substantive restrictions. The hardness derives from Huang–Ilango–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483).
solved_when: A reduction establishes conditional-Kolmogorov approximation hardness for algorithms running in time close to the input length, with the approximation gap and reduction overhead quantified.
why: It would connect this hardness to efficient compression and prediction, where near-linear time is the natural efficiency regime.
key_works: Huang–Ilango–Ren (2023/2025), [paper on conditional Kolmogorov complexity](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M1608483).

title: Nondeterministically secure WE from conventional assumptions
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Can witness encryption secure against nondeterministic distinguishers be built from well-studied, conventional cryptographic assumptions? A satisfying construction should state its circuit and advice bounds explicitly.
status: Strong witness encryption is known to supply range-avoidance consequences (Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061)), but a foundation from conventional assumptions remains a separate target.
solved_when: A construction of witness encryption secure against nondeterministic distinguishers is given, based on conventional assumptions, with explicit circuit and advice bounds.
why: It would give a conventional-assumption foundation for the range-avoidance consequences of strong WE, potentially yielding new search and proof-complexity lower bounds.
key_works: Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061).

title: Expressivity limits of nondeterministic WE
subfield: Learning theory, meta-complexity, and range avoidance
open: Which language classes can be witness-encrypted under a nondeterministic notion of WE security, and does this yield cryptographic consequences beyond those of ordinary witness encryption? A second sentence making it formal: classify the expressivity of nondeterministic WE and prove separations between it and standard WE.
status: This is a proposed classification target, motivated by recent range-avoidance applications, including Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); and Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061).
solved_when: A classification of the language classes achievable under nondeterministic WE security is established, together with proofs of separation (or equivalence) from ordinary witness encryption and an account of the cryptographic consequences it entails.
why: It clarifies whether a strong assumption has only narrow applications or carries broad structural consequences across cryptography and complexity.
key_works: Chen–Li (2023/2024), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Remote Point for Restricted Circuits via Cryptography](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/206/); Ren–Wang–Zhong (2025/2026), [Hardness of Range Avoidance and Proof Complexity Generators from Demi-Bits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14061).

title: Compact public validity with unique decryption
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Can a witness-encryption scheme support succinct public verification of ciphertext validity together with robust unique decryption, without paying the cost of general-purpose proofs? That is, can anyone check in public that a ciphertext is well-formed, while decryption remains unambiguous for all valid ciphertexts?
status: Basic unique-decryption witness encryption is already studied and constructed (Niu–Li–Huang–Liang–Tang (2015), [paper on unique-decryption WE](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-17533-1_38); Pan–Liang–Li–Ni (2019), [subsequent WE construction](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-21548-4_33)); compact publicly checkable validity remains the stronger, unachieved target.
solved_when: A construction is given (with security proof) whose ciphertexts admit a compact, publicly computable validity check and whose decryption is uniquely determined, avoiding full general-purpose proof overhead.
why: It prevents ambiguous or malformed encrypted rewards from being accepted, so encrypted outputs are publicly auditable without trusted parties.
key_works: Niu–Li–Huang–Liang–Tang (2015), [paper on unique-decryption WE](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-17533-1_38); Pan–Liang–Li–Ni (2019), [subsequent WE construction](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-21548-4_33).

title: Selective opening for condition portfolios
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Can an encryption scheme remain secure when an adversary adaptively forces some ciphertexts open, learning the underlying witnesses and encryption randomness, and then attacks the correlated conditions that remain unopened? Formally, establish a selective-opening security notion (and a scheme meeting it) for condition portfolios, where ordinary indistinguishability is insufficient.
status: Proposed as a WE-specific composition target; ordinary indistinguishability is known not to establish selective-opening security. Related foundational work includes Bellare–Dowsley–Waters–Yilek (2011), [selective-opening encryption research](https://eprint.iacr.org/2011/581), and Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).
solved_when: A precise selective-opening security definition for condition portfolios is formulated, together with a proof (or a construction with proof) that security holds against adversaries that adaptively open ciphertexts, obtain their witnesses and randomness, and attack correlated unopened conditions.
why: It would support portfolios of related escrows and archives, where related conditions must stay protected even after some are opened.
key_works: Bellare–Dowsley–Waters–Yilek (2011), [selective-opening encryption research](https://eprint.iacr.org/2011/581); Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).

title: Tight multi-instance adaptive soundness
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Can a cryptographic scheme hold tight security even when the adversary adaptively chooses and correlates many instances and sees many ciphertexts? More precisely, can we obtain security bounds that avoid losses proportional to every possible challenge position under adaptive multi-instance composition?
status: Adaptive witness encryption is established; tight quantitative composition remains the proposed frontier. Key work: Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).
solved_when: A tight security reduction is established for adaptively selected, correlated instances with many ciphertexts, with no loss factor proportional to the number of possible challenge positions.
why: It would let large services deploy these schemes without inflating parameters to compensate for reduction losses, keeping keys and ciphertexts practical at scale.
key_works: Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704).

title: Ciphertext-size lower bounds
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: How large must a ciphertext be? Prove lower bounds on ciphertext size as a function of the relation description, witness length, batch count, and security model, and show that universal and indexed settings are genuinely separated.
status: A lower-bound program has been proposed and sharpened by recent succinct batch and positional constructions, notably Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025/2026), [Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944); no lower bounds are yet established.
solved_when: Quantitative ciphertext-size lower bounds are proved in terms of the relation description, witness length, and batch count, in specified security models, with a demonstrated separation between the universal and indexed settings.
why: Such bounds distinguish engineering inefficiency from inherent representation cost, telling cryptographers when a shorter ciphertext is impossible rather than merely not yet achieved.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025/2026), [Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A machine-checked WE definition lattice
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Can the sprawling family of witness-encryption security definitions — adaptive, extractable, statistical, succinct, and quantum variants — be organized into a single machine-checked lattice of formal implication proofs, with the failed converses made explicit? In other words, a formalization where each provable implication is certified and each non-implication is recorded as such.
status: This is currently a proposed infrastructure target; the substantial definitional distinctions it would consolidate reside across separate papers, including Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704) and Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/).
solved_when: A proof-assistant formalization exists covering adaptive, extractable, statistical, succinct, and quantum variants of witness encryption, including machine-checked implication proofs and explicit failed converses, replacing the currently scattered paper-based distinctions.
why: Applications currently risk assuming guarantees their witness-encryption primitive does not actually provide; a machine-checked lattice makes such mismatches mechanically detectable.
key_works: Bellare–Hoang (2013/2015), [Adaptive Witness Encryption and Asymmetric Password-based Cryptography](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/704); Liu–Mazor–Pass (2024/2026), [On Witness Encryption and Laconic Zero-Knowledge Arguments](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/194/).

title: A witness-preserving reduction corpus
subfield: Security definitions and composability
open: Can we build an executable corpus of NP reductions that explicitly transform witnesses, track how witness sizes grow, and preserve the security-relevant distribution on instances? Such a corpus would make each reduction a checked artifact rather than a proof sketch.
status: Currently a proposed data target; existing decision-reduction collections omit the crucial WE requirements. Related to the context of Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).
solved_when: A data artifact exists containing executable NP reductions that (i) explicitly transform witnesses, (ii) track witness size growth, and (iii) preserve the security-relevant instance distribution.
why: It makes language specialization and comparisons between witness-encryption constructions reproducible; without it, ordinary decision-reduction collections omit the crucial witness-encryption requirements.
key_works: Goldberg–Kabanets (2025), [Witness Encryption and NP-Hardness of Learning](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.34).

title: The minimal exact-cover encoding interface
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Which graded-encoding operations are truly needed to build exact-cover witness encryption? In other words, determine the weakest concrete interface of multilinear-map operations for which exact-cover WE can be constructed and proven secure, dispensing with any functionality beyond what the scheme actually uses.
status: This is a proposed refinement of the 2013 Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters construction ([Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258)), motivated by the extensive attacks on general encoding candidates; related work includes Ma–Zhandry (2018), [The MMap Strikes Back](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/946).
solved_when: A precise interface specification is identified, together with a construction of exact-cover witness encryption from it and a security proof that relies only on assumptions about those operations — with no unnecessary general multilinear-map functionality invoked.
why: A restricted interface is likely easier to instantiate and to analyze than a full graded-encoding scheme, which matters given how fragile general candidates have proven.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), [Witness Encryption and its Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258); Ma–Zhandry (2018), [The MMap Strikes Back](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/946).

title: Reusable concrete encoding parameters
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Can witness encryption be instantiated with public encoding parameters that are fixed once and reused across many instances, while remaining secure against adversaries who adaptively choose instances and mount cross-ciphertext algebraic attacks?
status: Instance-independent assumptions trace back to Gentry–Lewko–Waters (2014), [Witness Encryption from Instance Independent Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/273); the more recent ordinary generic-group construction of Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275), instead uses fresh encodings.
solved_when: A witness encryption scheme is given whose encoding parameters are reusable — generated once and shared across instances — with a proof that security holds under adaptively chosen instances and cross-ciphertext algebraic attacks.
why: It removes the need to repeat an expensive setup for every condition, making witness encryption practical for settings where many instances are encrypted against.
key_works: Gentry–Lewko–Waters (2014), [Witness Encryption from Instance Independent Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/273); Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).

title: Specialize established iO to witness checking
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Can an established indistinguishability obfuscation scheme be specialized, with its assumptions and proofs intact, so that obfuscating witness-checking-and-release circuits avoids the overhead inherent to handling arbitrary programs?
status: This is currently a proposed efficiency target rather than a realized construction; it is known that general iO already implies witness encryption conditionally. Key works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1003); Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).
solved_when: A specialization of an established iO construction (e.g., Jain–Lin–Sahai or Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan) obfuscates witness-checking-and-release circuits with measurably reduced overhead relative to general-purpose obfuscation of the same circuits, while preserving the original construction's assumptions and security proofs.
why: Witness encryption could see substantial efficiency improvements without requiring any new foundational assumption beyond what general iO already rests on.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1003); Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: Separate the LPN ingredients
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Eliminate either large-field LPN or binary sparse LPN from the algebraic route to WE, or show why the two roles cannot be merged.
status: Proposed assumption-minimization target beyond the 2024 construction.
why: Simplifies security evaluation and reduces conjectural dependencies.
key_works: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: Malicious composition of annihilating FHE
subfield: Multilinear maps, iO, and FHE-derived constructions
open: Does the witness-encryption construction built from garbled circuits and multikey fully homomorphic encryption remain secure when keys, ciphertexts, and multiple executions are adversarially correlated? Formally, prove the required annihilation and hiding properties under such maliciously correlated inputs.
status: Currently a proposed strengthening; the individual component guarantees are known not to automatically establish the composed WE security game. Key work: Kluczniak (2020/2021), [Witness Encryption from Garbled Circuit and Multikey Fully Homomorphic Encryption Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1502).
solved_when: The annihilation and hiding properties are proved to hold under maliciously correlated keys, ciphertexts, and multiple executions, in a way that establishes the composed witness-encryption security game.
why: This would let the construction support adversarially supplied keys and ciphertexts and reusable services, rather than requiring honestly generated inputs for each execution.
key_works: Kluczniak (2020/2021), [Witness Encryption from Garbled Circuit and Multikey Fully Homomorphic Encryption Techniques](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1502).

title: S-oblivious private-coin evasive LWE
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: Are there useful S-oblivious private-coin evasive-LWE distributions that remain secure, or do counterexamples exist within the precise restrictions these formulations impose? Formally, establish security for such distributions or exhibit counterexamples satisfying their stated restrictions.
status: A 2026 analysis by Huang–Hung–Yamada (2026), [A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/4/20), narrows the attack landscape; the surviving restricted formulations are not automatically validated by it.
solved_when: Either a proof of security for a useful S-oblivious private-coin evasive-LWE distribution within its precise restrictions, or a counterexample satisfying those same restrictions, is given.
why: It tests whether a defensible lattice route to null-iO and witness encryption survives; a counterexample would break that route.
key_works: Huang–Hung–Yamada (2026), [A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/4/20).

title: Safe distributions for the auxiliary B matrix
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: Which distributions for the auxiliary B matrix are safe to use — that is, which ones preserve both evasive-LWE security and the functionality required for witness encryption? Formally, the goal is a characterization of the auxiliary-matrix distributions under which the evasive-LWE assumption remains sound while the intended construction still works.
status: The 2024–2025 definitions and counterexamples — Brzuska–Ünal–Woo (2024/2025), [Evasive LWE Assumptions: Definitions, Classes, and Counterexamples](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2000) — show that unrestricted formulations fail.
solved_when: A precise characterization of auxiliary-matrix distributions is given, identifying those that preserve both evasive-LWE security and the witness-encryption functionality, with proofs (or counterexamples) delimiting the boundary.
why: Without such a characterization, repairs to the assumption risk being too weak to support the intended witness-encryption construction, so the fix would silently fail.
key_works: Brzuska–Ünal–Woo (2024/2025), [Evasive LWE Assumptions: Definitions, Classes, and Counterexamples](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2000).

title: Bounded dependence on the LWE secret
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: How much dependence on the LWE secret can a sampling procedure have before the known obfuscation-based attacks on evasive LWE apply? Formally, characterize the boundary between benign and unsafe secret-dependent sampling.
status: The boundary question was proposed and sharpened by the 2026 S-oblivious analysis of Huang–Hung–Yamada (2026), [A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/4/20); it remains open.
solved_when: A quantitative characterization (e.g., a bound on the admissible secret-dependent sampling) is proved, delineating exactly when evasive-LWE attacks apply and when they provably do not.
why: It yields useful assumption classes interpolating between complete independence of the secret and unsafe dependence, expanding the design space for lattice-based cryptography.
key_works: Huang–Hung–Yamada (2026), [A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/4/20).

title: Public-coin noise-ordering security
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: Can we identify a choice of noise distribution and sampling order for which public-coin evasive LWE remains secure — in particular, resisting zeroizing attacks — while preserving the reduction to witness encryption? A formal answer would specify these parameters and prove that the resulting assumption excludes the known attack strategies.
status: The 2025 attacks (Agrawal–Modi–Yadav–Yamada (2025), [Zeroizing Attacks against Evasive and Circular Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/375)) expose sensitivity to the precise order and distribution of samples.
solved_when: Concrete noise and sampling orders are exhibited that (i) support public-coin evasive LWE, (ii) exclude zeroizing attacks, and (iii) retain the witness-encryption reduction.
why: It would make seemingly minor parameter choices part of a defensible assumption, rather than an ad hoc source of vulnerability.
key_works: Agrawal–Modi–Yadav–Yamada (2025), [Zeroizing Attacks against Evasive and Circular Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/375).

title: Genuinely public-coin circular evasive LWE
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: Is there a formulation of the circular evasive-LWE assumption whose sampling coins are genuinely public — with no hidden information smuggled back in through an auxiliary object — that is both useful for circular constructions and supported by evidence of hardness?
status: This is a proposed repair target after the 2025 zeroizing attacks, which exposed weaknesses in existing evasive and circular evasive LWE assumptions. Key work: Agrawal–Modi–Yadav–Yamada (2025), [Zeroizing Attacks against Evasive and Circular Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/375).
solved_when: A circular evasive-LWE assumption is stated with genuinely public sampling coins (no auxiliary object carrying secret information), and the assumption is validated as useful and plausibly hard.
why: It clarifies the actual trust and hardness premises behind circular constructions, which the 2025 zeroizing attacks showed to be on shaky ground.
key_works: Agrawal–Modi–Yadav–Yamada (2025), [Zeroizing Attacks against Evasive and Circular Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/375).

title: Complete parameterization of repaired lattice WE
subfield: Evasive LWE and repaired lattice assumptions
open: Can the repaired lattice-based witness encryption programme be carried through to a single, fully specified construction? That is, can one publish a scheme that fixes every distribution, dependency, error bound, reduction loss, and concrete parameter constraint end to end?
status: Currently this is a proposed engineering-theory target; eliminating one counterexample does not establish an end-to-end scheme. Key works: Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140); Brzuska–Ünal–Woo (2024/2025), [Evasive LWE Assumptions: Definitions, Classes, and Counterexamples](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2000).
solved_when: A complete repaired construction is published that explicitly specifies every distribution, every dependency, every error bound, the reduction loss, and all concrete parameter constraints — an end-to-end scheme, not merely the elimination of an individual counterexample.
why: It enables independent cryptanalysis and meaningful cost estimates for the scheme, neither of which is possible while only fragments and repairs are specified.
key_works: Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140); Brzuska–Ünal–Woo (2024/2025), [Evasive LWE Assumptions: Definitions, Classes, and Counterexamples](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2000).

title: Noncommuting ADP blocks against sparse-commutator attacks
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can we design determinant-program encodings whose noncommuting blocks provably resist sparse-commutator attacks, while still admitting efficient witness evaluation? Formally, the goal is a construction that combines noncommuting block structure with a security argument against these attacks.
status: The problem arises as a proposed repair following the 2026 cryptanalysis; as yet, noncommutativity alone is not a security proof. Key works: El Gebali et al. (2026), [Breaking ADP-Based Witness Encryption](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1594); Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf).
solved_when: A determinant-program encoding with noncommuting blocks is constructed that defeats sparse-commutator attacks and preserves efficient witness evaluation, ideally with a security argument showing noncommutativity suffices against these attacks.
why: A solution would test whether the ADP approach has a viable successor after the 2026 cryptanalysis.
key_works: El Gebali et al. (2026), [Breaking ADP-Based Witness Encryption](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1594); Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf).

title: Determinant-preserving masks with defensible hiding
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can we build masking transformations for determinant programs that preserve the required determinant predicate while leaving an adversary no exploitable invariants of the original program? Formally, the mask must satisfy the determinant condition exactly and resist invariant-based cryptanalysis.
status: Natural masking approaches are constrained by attacks from 2022 and 2026, notably Yao–Chen–Yu (2022), [Cryptanalysis of Candidate Obfuscators for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/1684).
solved_when: A construction of masking transformations is given that provably preserves the determinant predicate and for which the known attack techniques against natural masking approaches no longer apply.
why: It addresses the core hiding requirement of determinant-program obfuscation directly, rather than patching weaknesses at the compiler level.
key_works: Yao–Chen–Yu (2022), [Cryptanalysis of Candidate Obfuscators for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/1684).

title: QAP densification with a proved rank gap
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can QAP-derived determinant programs be densified in a way that provably preserves the intended rank gap between satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances, so that known low-rank attacks fail? In other words, is there a densification procedure with a proof that the satisfiable/unsatisfiable rank separation survives and that MinRank-style solvers cannot exploit the structure?
status: The problem was posed as a proposed response to 2026 structural attacks and accompanying repair suggestions. Key works: Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf); Soukhanov et al. (2026), [Implementable Witness Encryption from Arithmetic Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/175).
solved_when: A densification method for QAP-derived determinant programs is given, together with a proof that the intended satisfiable/unsatisfiable rank gap is preserved and that known low-rank attacks fail against the densified programs.
why: It would connect the algebraic repair proposals prompted by recent structural attacks to actual NP reductions, turning heuristic fixes into provably secure compilation of arithmetic circuits into determinant programs (e.g., for witness encryption).
key_works: Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf); Soukhanov et al. (2026), [Implementable Witness Encryption from Arithmetic Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/175).

title: Projectively safe arithmetic compilation
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can arithmetic conditions be compiled into determinant programs in a way that never introduces projective or homogenization artifacts — that is, unintended accepting assignments arising from the compilation itself?
status: This is currently a proposed correctness-and-security target around the 2026 implementable candidate, described in Soukhanov et al. (2026), [Implementable Witness Encryption from Arithmetic Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/175); no compilation procedure meeting the target is known.
solved_when: A compilation procedure exists that transforms a given arithmetic condition into a determinant program with no projective or homogenization artifacts creating unintended accepting assignments, so the encrypted condition exactly matches the intended verifier.
why: Without such a compiler, the determinant program may accept witnesses the original condition rejects, breaking soundness of the arithmetization and of any verifier built on it.
key_works: Soukhanov et al. (2026), [Implementable Witness Encryption from Arithmetic Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/175).

title: Defensible ADP block-size parameters
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can we determine block-size and ciphertext-size requirements for ADP-based schemes that provably withstand all known algebraic attacks? In particular, can these requirements be derived together with independently reproduced estimates of the cost of each attack?
status: September 2026 discussions include very large conjectural parameter estimates, but these are not validated secure deployment records. Key works: Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf); Jo (2026), [Cryptanalysis of a Candidate Witness Encryption Scheme for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1583).
solved_when: Block-size and ciphertext-size parameters are derived against all known algebraic attacks, and the attack costs are independently reproduced — yielding a validated, defensible parameter set rather than conjectural estimates.
why: It determines whether repaired ADP schemes could ever be economical: if secure parameters force impractically large blocks or ciphertexts, the approach is dead on efficiency grounds.
key_works: Towa (2026), [Swiss Crypto Day slides](https://swisscryptoday.github.io/assets/2026-09/talks/PatricTowa.pdf); Jo (2026), [Cryptanalysis of a Candidate Witness Encryption Scheme for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1583).

title: Instance-independent assumptions for repaired ADP WE
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can a repaired ADP-based witness encryption scheme be founded on an explicit instance-independent assumption that remains meaningful even when adversaries select the programs? Formally, the goal is to replace ad hoc, instance-by-instance hardness claims with a single reusable assumption covering adversarially chosen affine determinant programs.
status: This is currently a proposed foundational target. Surviving individual examples of the scheme do not establish universal hardness, so no instance-independent assumption is yet in place. Related context: Jo (2026), [Cryptanalysis of a Candidate Witness Encryption Scheme for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1583); Gentry–Lewko–Waters (2014), [Witness Encryption from Instance Independent Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/273).
solved_when: A repaired ADP scheme is proven secure under an explicitly stated instance-independent assumption that holds across adversarially selected programs, rather than only for surviving individual examples.
why: A solution unlocks reusable parameters and a coherent, uniform security claim, instead of security arguments that must be re-established for each instance.
key_works: Jo (2026), [Cryptanalysis of a Candidate Witness Encryption Scheme for Affine Determinant Programs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1583); Gentry–Lewko–Waters (2014), [Witness Encryption from Instance Independent Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/273).

title: Reuse one prime-order generic encoding
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can a prime-order generic-group witness-encryption scheme be reused across many adaptively chosen ciphertexts that all share a single encoding, without losing the proof? Formally, extend the construction so one generic encoding supports multiple adaptive encryptions while preserving security.
status: The September 2026 ordinary construction uses a fresh random encoding per encryption and classical oracle queries. Key work: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).
solved_when: A construction is given that handles many adaptively chosen ciphertexts sharing one encoding while preserving the proof, replacing the current fresh-random-encoding-per-encryption approach.
why: It moves the idealized construction toward reusable public infrastructure.
key_works: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).

title: Polynomial-gap Boolean-factor homogeneous MinRank
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can homogeneous MinRank be proven hard even when the instances have Boolean factor structure and only a polynomial multiplicative gap is required? That is, establish the homogeneous MinRank hardness assumption needed for these applications in the polynomial-gap, Boolean-factor regime.
status: The 2026 construction establishes a logarithmic-gap route; broader announced improvements must be distinguished from completed proofs. Key work: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).
solved_when: A proof of homogeneous MinRank hardness is obtained for instances with Boolean factor structure under a polynomial multiplicative gap.
why: A solution could improve the efficiency of group-based witness encryption and strengthen the assumptions it rests on.
key_works: Hair–Sahai (2026), [Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18275).

title: Superlogarithmic GapMDP for polynomial-size circuits
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Obtain the matrix-decision gap needed for the SNARG-and-groups route on polynomial-size circuits, with polynomial-security assumptions.
status: The 2026 result uses restricted circuit sizes and subexponential SNARG security; the unrestricted target remains.
why: Broadens the language and parameter range of a distinct construction route.
key_works: Barta et al. (2020), [On Succinct Arguments and Witness Encryption from Groups](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-56784-2_26); Jin (2026), [Witness Encryption for NP from SNARGs and Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2063).

title: Concrete instantiation of generic-group extractable WE
subfield: Determinant programs, MinRank, and generic groups
open: Can the October 2026 generic-group extractable witness encryption claim be realized in concrete groups, with an explicit and defensible extraction assumption? Formally, is there an instantiation whose extractability can be justified outside the idealized generic-group oracle model?
status: Generic-group extraction is a recent claimed milestone, but concrete security remains a separate, unresolved question. Key works: Campanelli (2026), [A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399); Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).
solved_when: A concrete-group instantiation of the generic-group EWE construction is given, together with an explicitly stated extraction assumption that is defensible outside the generic-group model.
why: It would make the hard-true applications of extractable witness encryption assessable with real security rather than only relative to an idealized oracle.
key_works: Campanelli (2026), [A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399); Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).

title: The minimal KOALA fragment needed for WE
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: What is the weakest restricted KOALA-style knowledge premise that still supports useful extractable witness encryption? A formal answer would pin down the minimal fragment — with no unnecessary obfuscation or sampler power — that suffices.
status: The problem was posed as a minimization target following the October 2026 public-coin diO result, building on Beullens–Wee (2019), [Obfuscating Simple Functionalities from Knowledge Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/056), and Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346); no minimal fragment has yet been isolated.
solved_when: A restricted KOALA fragment is identified and shown sufficient for useful EWE, with a proof that any weaker version (dropping obfuscation or sampler power beyond the identified minimum) fails to suffice.
why: It shrinks the conjectural extraction claim that must withstand cryptanalysis to its smallest credible form, directly reducing the assumption's attack surface.
key_works: Beullens–Wee (2019), [Obfuscating Simple Functionalities from Knowledge Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/056); Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).

title: Maximal safe auxiliary-input classes
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Which classes of auxiliary information can be safely allowed alongside extractable witness encryption, so that extraction still works without falling into known impossibility arguments? More precisely, characterize the useful auxiliary-information classes that admit EWE extraction while avoiding the barriers established for arbitrary advice.
status: This has been a frontier since the 2014–2015 auxiliary-input critiques: arbitrary advice cannot simply be permitted, as shown by Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), [On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/860), and Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).
solved_when: A characterization (explicit description) of auxiliary-information classes is given for which EWE extraction holds, together with a proof that these classes evade the Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs and Boyle–Pass impossibility arguments.
why: Real applications expose correlated public information and prior ciphertexts, so identifying safe auxiliary-input classes determines when extractable witness encryption can be deployed beyond the bare-auxiliary setting.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), [On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/860); Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).

title: Composition with EWE-derived auxiliary information
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Does extraction remain sound when the adversary's later instances and auxiliary advice may depend on earlier EWE ciphertexts, outputs, or previously extracted witnesses? Formally, can single-instance extractability be lifted to a setting of recursive, dependent invocations of the primitive?
status: Currently a proposed composition target; it is recognized that single-instance restrictions need not remain valid under recursive use. Key works: Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of extraction is obtained for adversaries whose later instances and advice depend on earlier EWE ciphertexts, outputs, or extracted witnesses, replacing the single-instance restriction currently assumed.
why: It underpins chains of escrows and other proof-dependent applications, where single-instance guarantees do not obviously survive recursive use.
key_works: Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).

title: Restricted EWE-to-SNARG barrier boundaries
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Which consequences of extractable witness encryption still yield SNARGs once we restrict to the settings already covered by existing impossibility theorems? A precise answer would map how adaptivity, uniqueness, completeness error, and setup assumptions each shift the boundary.
status: The 2026 unique-SNARG results sharply distinguish perfect completeness from negligible completeness error; a generic "all SNARGs are impossible" reading is incorrect. Key works: Gentry–Wichs (2011), [Separating Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments From All Falsifiable Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2010/610); Freitag–Wichs (2026), [Unique SNARGs with Adaptive Security: Constructions and Black-Box Separations](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/881).
solved_when: A characterization exists of which restricted EWE-to-SNARG constructions remain possible, delineated by adaptivity, uniqueness, completeness error (perfect versus negligible), and setup, consistent with the known impossibility theorems.
why: It sharpens the extractability-versus-falsifiability debate by pinning down exactly where extractability assumptions stop helping beyond falsifiable ones.
key_works: Gentry–Wichs (2011), [Separating Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments From All Falsifiable Assumptions](https://eprint.iacr.org/2010/610); Freitag–Wichs (2026), [Unique SNARGs with Adaptive Security: Constructions and Black-Box Separations](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/881).

title: Rewinding-free extraction from concrete encodings
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Can we build extractable witness encryption for expressive languages where extraction is straight-line and works over concrete groups, even against adversaries making concurrent adaptive statements, and without assuming adversaries admit algebraic representations? In other words, is there an EWE scheme whose extractor needs no rewinding and relies on no algebraic-representation assumption on the adversary?
status: The problem is posed as a strengthening beyond existing algebraic and generic-group extraction models; the reference point is Fleischhacker–Hall-Andersen–Simkin (2024), [Extractable Witness Encryption for KZG Commitments and Efficient Laconic OT](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/264). No such construction is recorded.
solved_when: A construction of special-language extractable witness encryption is given whose extraction is straight-line in the concrete-group (not generic- or algebraic-model) setting and remains sound under concurrent adaptive statement queries, with no assumption of adversarial algebraic representations.
why: It would simplify reductions for concurrent applications and support quantum-aware settings, where rewinding-based extraction typically fails.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Hall-Andersen–Simkin (2024), [Extractable Witness Encryption for KZG Commitments and Efficient Laconic OT](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/264).

title: Restricted private-coin upgrades to extractability
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Can the public-coin extractability-with-extractability (EWE) or differing-input obfuscation (diO) construction be upgraded to handle private-coin statement samplers — that is, samplers whose statement generation uses hidden randomness — without reintroducing the prohibited auxiliary information?
status: This is a proposed frontier following the October 2026 public-coin construction; the public-coin qualifier cannot be dropped automatically. Key work: Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).
solved_when: A construction is given that achieves useful private-coin statement samplers for public-coin EWE or diO while provably excluding the prohibited auxiliary information.
why: It would extend extractability guarantees to natural applications whose statement generation inherently uses hidden randomness, which the current public-coin setting cannot cover.
key_works: Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).

title: Functional WE below full diO
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: Which witness-dependent functions f(message, witness) admit functional witness encryption under assumptions strictly weaker than general differing-inputs obfuscation? More formally, characterize the restricted closure classes of functions for which functional witness encryption can be built without assuming full extractability obfuscation.
status: General functional witness encryption has established connections to obfuscation; restricted closure classes are the proposed target for weakening the assumption. Key reference: Boyle–Chung–Pass (2014), [On Extractability (a.k.a. Differing-Inputs) Obfuscation](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/650).
solved_when: A characterization is given of the witness-dependent functions admitting functional witness encryption under an assumption weaker than general differing-inputs obfuscation, together with a construction for those restricted closure classes (or a proof that no such characterization exists below full diO).
why: It would allow controlled witness-dependent outputs without assuming maximal extractability, keeping the required trust in assumptions proportionate to what the application actually needs.
key_works: Boyle–Chung–Pass (2014), [On Extractability (a.k.a. Differing-Inputs) Obfuscation](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/650).

title: Advice-size thresholds for extractability
subfield: Extractability and knowledge-assumption boundaries
open: How much auxiliary advice can an extractor's setting tolerate before extraction assumptions become vacuous? More precisely, identify the advice-size thresholds that separate settings where extraction is still constructible from those large enough to encode known counterexamples.
status: Proposed as a quantitative question following the 2015 observation that circuits can absorb bounded advice, per Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).
solved_when: A quantitative characterization of advice budgets is given, separating constructible extraction settings from advice sizes capable of encoding the known counterexamples.
why: It makes "no auxiliary input" claims in extraction assumptions operationally meaningful rather than merely formal.
key_works: Boyle–Pass (2015), [Limits of Extractability Assumptions with Distributional Auxiliary Input](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/703).

title: Functional-commitment WE beyond NC¹
subfield: Special languages, commitments, and SNARK gadgets
open: Can succinct functional-commitment witness encryption be extended beyond NC¹ to richer classes of functions? In particular, is there such a scheme for an explicitly larger circuit class, with concrete efficiency and assumption bounds stated?
